Title: Students want say in law replacing AUKU
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Student leaders have welcomed the government's decision to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU), but want students to have a meaningful say in drafting the legislation that replaces it.
Universiti Malaya student representative Syam Eddy Ahmad, a second-year Environmental Studies student, described the repeal as a long-awaited victory for the student movement, saying AUKU had historically restricted student autonomy and academic freedom.
"I support the repeal. But there must be a framework to replace AUKU, and the new Act must be more student-friendly.
"Students themselves must be involved in drafting it, together with academics and universities," he said.
Syam said legislation governing higher education remained necessary to ensure continuity in university administration, but the replacement law should not undermine student autonomy or allow political appointments to influence university governance.
He also welcomed greater political participation among students, saying campus movements could help strengthen democratic culture.
"More students may become involved in politics and that will enliven democracy both on campus and nationally," he said.
Universiti Putra Malaysia Sarawak Campus student representative Freddie anak Andrew Sanggai, 22, however, said AUKU should not necessarily be discarded wholesale, as some provisions remained relevant.
"From my perspective as a student representative, AUKU is still relevant. However, there are parts that need to be updated," said Freddie, a second-year Human Development with Management student.
He said any new law should be drafted through consultations involving student representatives, academics and university administrations.
On political participation, Freddie said students should be encouraged to understand and engage in politics, but should remember that their primary purpose at university was to pursue their education.
Universiti Sains Malaysia Student Parliament Speaker and president of the Student Representative Council at the Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Engineering Campus, Muhammad Nuraiman Mohd Yusrino, said the debate over AUKU reflected a broader question of university autonomy and how much trust should be placed in students to shape their future.
He said although amendments to AUKU had provided greater space for student participation, the repeal offered an opportunity to reconsider whether an Act created more than five decades ago remained suitable for today's higher education landscape.
"The real question is whether the higher education legal framework should continue to be built around an Act that was created more than five decades ago, in a very different context," he said.
Nuraiman said repealing AUKU did not mean universities would be left without rules or students given unrestricted freedom.
Instead, he said, it should pave the way for a modern framework that balances institutional autonomy with accountability and the public interest.
"Democracy will not mature if people are never given the opportunity to practise it. Leadership will also not develop if students are only allowed to make decisions within a very limited space," he said.
Nuraiman said students should be involved in developing the new framework alongside the ministry, universities, academics, administrators, industry and wider society.
"Students should not merely be the party receiving decisions. Students need to be part of the decision-making process," he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had announced on Aug 15 that AUKU would be repealed to provide students with greater freedom and wider democratic space.
The Higher Education Ministry Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir had said the replacement framework would be developed through the One Higher Education Act approach, involving an independent committee, extensive stakeholder consultations and a transition mechanism to ensure university governance and operations continue without disruption.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police arrest 5, seize RM12.8mil in two smuggling operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested five people and seized contraband and other goods worth RM12.8 million in two operations targeting suspected smuggling in Kuala Lumpur and Klang.
Federal police Internal Security and Public Order (Operations) deputy director Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said the operations targeted suspected smuggling activities and breaches of import regulations involving liquor, cigarettes, helmets, beauty products and phone accessories.
He said Op Taring Alpha 2 on Aug 5 led to the arrest of three people, comprising two Myanmar citizens and a local.
Raids at two locations in Kuala Lumpur resulted in the seizure of various brands of liquor as well as food and beverage products from China, with a total value of about RM5.1 million.
"Among the items seized were 112 cans and 3,696 bottles of various brands of liquor worth about RM2.57 million, as well as 4,092 bottles of liquor worth about RM2.7 million.
"Various food and beverage products from China worth about RM56,000 were also seized," he said at a press conference at Bukit Aman.
Muhammad said Op Taring Alpha 5 in Klang, meanwhile, led to the arrest of two men and the seizure of various goods worth about RM7.7 million.
He said the seizure included Chinese liquor worth RM2.1 million, 245 cartons of white cigarettes, or 49,000 sticks, worth nearly RM300,000, and 1,800 helmets worth RM1.8 million.
"We also seized 780 sets of phone accessories worth RM936,000, beauty products worth RM2.29 million, as well as 260 potted bonsai trees of various sizes and types worth RM260,000," he said.
He said preliminary investigations found that both premises were believed to have been used as temporary storage and collection centres before the goods were distributed to local customers.
"Most of the goods are believed to have been brought in through ports using documents declaring contents that differed from the actual goods, while the activities are believed to have been operating for more than six months," he said.
Muhammad said the success of both operations was the result of cooperation between the police and various enforcement agencies through information and intelligence sharing.
He said from January to Aug 21 this year, the police Internal Security and Public Order Department had conducted 240 raids nationwide, resulting in 413 arrests and seizures worth a total of RM315 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia rejects US claim over transshipment of Chinese goods
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia denied a recent US report claiming its involvement in the transshipment of goods, the country's senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto said in a statement on Thursday.
Below are the details:
Airlangga was referring to a report released by Washington, which claimed the US is losing some US$19 billion to US$26 billion in annual tariff revenue to goods, largely from China, that are transshipped through third countries, including Indonesia, to avoid US import duties.
"Indonesia has been accused, along with Brazil, Malaysia, Thailand, Turkiye, and Vietnam, of being part of a global transshipment network. We state that these accusations are not true," the minister said.
He added that "it is not true that transshipment from other countries is being used for processing here."--REUTERS

Title: Rapid KL to run trains, selected buses 24 hours for National Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL will extend the operating hours of its rail and selected bus services to 24 hours from Aug 30 to 31 to support National Day 2026 celebrations.
"Aimed at easing public movement during the Merdeka period, the move will cover all rail services, including the Light Rail Transit (LRT), Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Kuala Lumpur Monorail.
"Train frequency will be increased on several key routes to accommodate higher passenger volumes, with schedules adjusted based on demand and real-time station conditions," Prasarana Malaysia Bhd said in a statement today.
Additional trains will also be deployed as needed to manage platform congestion. The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Sunway Line, several bus routes and the Rapid KL On-Demand (ROD) service will similarly operate around the clock.
"The extended hours are meant to ensure smoother movement for those attending the Ambang Merdeka celebration on the night of Aug 30, as well as the National Day event in Putrajaya on the morning of Aug 31," it said.
To support movement to the main celebration site, the operator will provide 103 free shuttle buses across two main routes.
The MS01 route will run from Putrajaya Sentral to Precinct 2, while the MS02 route will connect the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) to Precinct 3.
"The free shuttle service is intended to ease public access to the celebration area, reduce reliance on private vehicles and help ease traffic congestion around Putrajaya.
"More than 5,000 frontline personnel from various units will be deployed across shifts to manage crowd movement and ensure passenger flow runs smoothly and safely," it said.
Rapid KL also advised the public to use public transport to reach National Day venues to help mitigate traffic congestion in the city.
"Passengers are also advised to plan their journeys early, ensure sufficient balance on their Touch 'n Go cards and comply with the instructions of personnel, particularly at stations and areas with high passenger density," it said.

Title: Melaka polls: PN ready to forgo BN cooperation if it chooses PH, says Hadi
Article:
MARANG: Perikatan Nasional is prepared to forego cooperation with Barisan Nasional in the Melaka state election if the latter chooses to work with Pakatan Harapan.
Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said that while the PN coalition was confident it could pursue alternative strategies, discussions were still ongoing among its leaders, particularly on cooperation with BN for the Melaka state election.
He said no final decision had been made, although a majority of BN leaders were understood to favour continuing cooperation with PN.
"We have been informed that the BN leadership remains divided and hesitant, even though the majority of the party's leaders agree that cooperation with PN should continue," he said after delivering his Dhuha lecture at Masjid Rusila today.
Hadi said Pas and PN had several strategies and alternatives to strengthen Malay and Islamic political unity, as well as cooperation with non-extreme non-Muslim parties.
"Pas is confident that the negotiation process and the formation of political cooperation ahead of the Melaka state election will be easier compared with the situation during the Johor state election on July 11," he said.
He said the confidence was based on feedback and positive responses received at the grassroots level, taking into account the current national political scenario.
"The situation in the Johor state election was more complicated, but the path and conditions in Melaka are easier," he said.

Title: Security guard jailed 8 years, caned twice for sexually assaulting 10-year-old boy
Article:
MUAR: A security guard was sentenced to eight years in prison and two strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court here today for physically sexually assaulting a 10-year-old boy at a resource centre last month.
Judge Emelia Kaswati Mohamad Khalid sentenced Muzaffar Shah Jaamat, 31, after he pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The court also ordered the accused to undergo counselling while in prison and police supervision after completing his sentence, in accordance with Sections 26 and 27 of the same Act.
According to the charge, the accused, who is due to marry early next year, committed the offence against the 10-year-old boy at a resource centre in Batu Pahat at about 3.30pm in July.
Section 14(d) provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, a police report was lodged at 12.51pm on Monday after the school received a call about a pupil being subjected to an indecent act.
Police investigations found that the victim and the accused knew each other and often played games on their mobile phones at the resource centre.
While at the resource centre, the accused pulled down the victim's trousers and removed them.
The victim later told his class teacher about the incident.
Acting on the information, police arrested the accused at a school at 8.50pm on the same day while he was working as a security guard.
Deputy public prosecutor Amirah Sapian appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: LYC Healthcare aims Aug 28 release of delayed annual report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: LYC Healthcare Bhd is targeting Aug 28 to issue its delayed annual report for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26), as outstanding audit matters involving a disposed subsidiary and accounting treatments remain unresolved.
The healthcare group, whose shares have been suspended from trading since Aug 10 over the delay, said the audit is now in its final stages.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, LYC said the delay was primarily due to its inability to obtain timely access to records and information from Elite Dental Team Sdn Bhd, which it disposed of on Dec 31, 2024.
This created difficulties for external auditor SBY Partners PLT in completing the necessary audit procedures as the firm was not Elite Dental's auditor during the reporting period.
LYC disclosed the details in response to a Bursa query seeking information on the progress of the audit, outstanding matters hindering its completion and a specific date for the issuance of the annual report.
The company said three matters remain outstanding, including the completion of audit work on Elite Dental and a review of the basis and supporting information for profit recognised in retained earnings.
The auditor is also completing adjustments relating to LYC's right-of-use assets and finalising certain accounting treatments involving deferred tax liability arising from the reconciliation of intercompany balances.
SBY Partners has tentatively targeted board approval of the financial statements on or before Aug 28, subject to LYC management's full cooperation in resolving the outstanding matters.
LYC consequently expects to issue its FY26 annual report by the same date and said it would immediately announce any change to the target.
LYC had initially expected to issue the annual report by Aug 7 after appointing SBY Partners as its new external auditor on March 6, replacing Crowe Malaysia PLT, which resigned on Feb 26 following a disagreement over audit fees.
On Aug 5, SBY Partners informed LYC's board and management that the financial statements were still under review and expected to finalise them by Aug 10.
The auditor subsequently said on Aug 10 that it required more time and expected to finalise the draft financial statements between Aug 17 and Aug 19.
On Aug 17, SBY Partners requested further information and supporting documents, which LYC said it provided on the same day.
As of Aug 19, the audit remained subject to the completion and clearance of outstanding audit procedures and further review by SBY Partners.
LYC's shares were suspended from trading on Aug 10 after it failed to issue its FY26 annual report within the prescribed timeframe.
The company had missed the July 31 deadline for issuing the report, which includes its audited financial statements and auditors' and directors' reports.
Under Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market Listing Requirements, the suspension will remain in effect until further notice. LYC could also face delisting procedures if the annual report remains outstanding for six months from the expiry of the relevant timeframe.

Title: Haze worsens in Sarawak as unhealthy API readings rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality nationwide has worsened, with more areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as haze from various directions moves into the state.
The Environment Department has stepped up enforcement and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning while monitoring API readings.
In a statement today, the department said one area recorded very unhealthy air quality while nine recorded unhealthy levels, all in Sarawak.
Another 56 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings, while two recorded good levels.
Serian district police headquarters recorded the country's highest API reading at 227, followed by Sri Aman (187), Kuching (176), Samarahan (175) and Sarikei (174).
Other unhealthy readings were recorded in Sibu (157), Bintulu (154), Samalaju (154), Kapit (130) and Mukah (130).
The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) detected 288 hotspots in Kalimantan and 53 in Sumatra on Aug 20, compared with two in Malaysia, one each in Sarawak and Terengganu.
Its regional haze map today showed moderate to dense transboundary smoke from West Kalimantan moving northwards into western Sarawak.
The department has activated the National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan to coordinate the government's response.
Under the haze action plan, outdoor classroom activities must stop when the API reading exceeds 100.
Meanwhile, schools, kindergartens and childcare centres must close when readings exceed 200.
Disaster management committees will be activated if readings exceed 150 for more than 24 hours.
Cloud seeding may also be carried out when readings exceed 150, subject to suitable weather conditions.
Landowners are urged to monitor fire-prone areas and prevent open burning. Offences carry fines of between RM25,000 and RM1 million, up to five years' jail, or both.
Earlier, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia was preparing for a stronger
El Nino
that could bring more severe haze.
At transboundary haze meetings in Bali on July 8 and 9, Malaysia also joined Brunei, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste in reviewing measures to prevent forest and land fires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singaporean security guard jailed 14 days, fined RM7,000 for insulting Islam
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A Singaporean security guard was sentenced to 14 days in jail and fined RM7,000 by the magistrates' court here today after pleading guilty to insulting Islam last month.
Magistrate A. Shaarmini ordered Mohamed Anim Atam, 56, to serve the jail term from the date of his arrest on Tuesday.
The court also ordered him to serve an additional three months in jail if he failed to pay the fine.
According to the charge, Mohamed Anim intentionally uttered words with the intention of wounding the religious feelings of others by making remarks deemed insulting to Islam, which were heard by a man.
He committed the offence while travelling from Jalan Tun Razak to Jalan Meldrum here about 5pm on July 30.
He was charged under Section 298 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum one-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, Mohamed Anim had said: "If the Quran is really true, if you study it, it's a very dangerous book of killing. All it does is kill, kill, kill. There is no compassion. All this is a lie. I don't believe it."
The complainant, who heard the remarks, later uploaded a video recording of the incident to several of his social media accounts before lodging a police report on July 31.
Deputy public prosecutor Eizlan Azhar urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, saying the case had gone viral on social media and involved a 3R issue.
In mitigation, the unrepresented accused appealed for a lighter sentence, saying he suffered from high blood pressure and was in the process of a divorce, which required him to attend proceedings at the Syariah Court in his country.
Earlier, a video showing the Singaporean allegedly insulting Islam while travelling in an e-hailing car around the city went viral on social media.
Following this, the suspect was arrested by a team from the Criminal Investigation Division of the Johor Baru Selatan district police headquarters, with the assistance of the Singapore Police Force.
Police also seized a mobile phone from the suspect to assist in investigations.

Title: Two Malaysians held in Thailand with 1,560 Epam tablets
Article:
SUNGAI GOLOK: Two Malaysians were arrested by Thai police after they were allegedly found in possession of 1,560 Epam tablets in Sungai Golok last night.
Sungai Golok police chief Police Colonel Than Sirikhan said the two men, aged 24 and 30, were detained at about 10.30pm along Anukachart Usorn Road.
He said the arrests were carried out by personnel from the Sungai Golok police station's Rapid Response Unit and Wihok Network Unit in front of Ban Boss Restaurant.
"Acting on public tip-offs, the team went to the area and arrested the two suspects.
"Checks found 1,560 tablets packed in 39 blister packs, with 40 tablets in each pack, valued at about 10,608 baht (RM862)."
Than said the suspects were being investigated for jointly possessing a Category 2 psychotropic substance, Epam (Nitrazepam 5mg), for the purpose of unauthorised sale.
"They were also being investigated for entering and remaining in Thailand without permission," he added.
He said the suspects and the seized items had been taken to investigators at Sungai Golok police station for further action.
It is learnt that the two Malaysian suspects had recently crossed into Sungai Golok town via one of the illegal jetties along the Kelantan-Thailand border in Rantau Panjang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 10 GOF personnel arrested over alleged Penang e-waste factory extortion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ten General Operations Force (GOF) personnel have been arrested to assist in investigations following an extortion case involving an e-waste processing factory in Tasek Gelugor, Penang.
The incident occurred on Wednesday, Federal police Internal Security and Public Order (Operations) deputy director Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said.
"We can confirm that there have been arrests. The matter is still under investigation and is under the action of the state police.
"Those detained were aged between 30 and 40, with the highest-ranking among them being an inspector and the lowest-ranking a constable," he said at a press conference at Bukit Aman.
They were subsequently remanded for one day to assist in the investigation.
Also present were Federal Police Internal Security and Public Order Department (GOF) deputy director Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi and Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar.
Muhammad said appropriate action would be taken against any personnel found to be involved in criminal activities.
"There will be no exceptions or preferential treatment," he said.

Title: Malaysian airports see 9.3pct jump in international traffic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: International traffic across Malaysian airports rose 9.3 per cent month-on-month to 4.5 million movements in July.
This was supported by the summer travel season across Europe, the Middle East and parts of Asia, according to Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB).
MAHB also saw connectivity expansion during the month with the introduction of two new airlines at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
AirBorneo commenced twice-daily direct services from Kuching to Kuala Lumpur on
July 20 and daily service from Kuching to Singapore on July 22, followed by Riyadh Air, which launched three-times-weekly direct services from Riyadh to Kuala Lumpur on July 31.
Overall, the group's local network handled eight million passenger movements in July, an increase of 4.6 per cent from June 2026.
Domestic traffic remained softer at 3.5 million passengers, declining 1.0 per cent from June and 19.8 per cent versus July 2025, as airlines continued to optimise capacity in response to operating costs and changing market demand.
Overall passenger movements across the airports in Malaysia were 11 per cent lower year-on-year (YoY) in July.
For the first seven months of 2026, MAHB's operations in Malaysia handled 59 million passengers, broadly comparable with the corresponding period last year.
International traffic grew 6.1 per cent YoY during the period, while domestic traffic dropped 6.7 per cent.
Year-to-date traffic at KLIA reached 36.7 million passengers, 3.4 per cent higher than the same period in 2025.
MAHB managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said international traffic continues to provide a positive counterbalance to softer domestic movements.
"While passenger traffic will vary across markets and periods, our focus remains on strengthening connectivity and ensuring that our airports are ready to support changing travel demand.
"At the same time, we continue to improve the passenger journey across our network.
"These improvements, together with the addition of new airline services, are part of the ongoing work to make our airports easier and more convenient to travel through," he said.
Beyond KLIA, Sultan Ismail Petra Airport (KBR) continued to build its international traffic following the introduction of the Kota Bharu–Jakarta service in June.
International passenger movements at KBR rose to more than 6,200 in July, an increase of 54.1 per cent from the preceding month.
Additionally check-in and baggage tag printing services were introduced at Sama-Sama Hotel KLIA.
This allows eligible passengers to complete part of the departure process before proceeding to the terminal for baggage drop.
Across the group, passenger traffic reached 12.8 million movements in July.
Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen International Airport recorded 4.9 million passengers during the month, an increase of 14.2 per cent from June and 9.6 per cent YoY.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan returned to jail after medical checkup
Article:
ISTANBUL: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was returned to jail after a medical examination at a health facility in the capital, Islamabad, following court orders, a senior official said Friday, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
Without naming Khan, 73, Pakistani Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said: "In the light of the Supreme Court's decision, the prisoner (Imran Khan) was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the intervening night of August 20 and 21, 2026."
"A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit," Tarar said in a statement on X.
He added that Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, "remained present throughout all stages of the medical examination/treatment."
"After the completion of this entire process, he was transferred back to Adiala Jail  approximately 5am local time (0000GMT)" on Friday, said the minister.
The medical examination of Khan, founder of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, was conducted after the Pakistani Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered prison authorities to transfer the former prime minister, who was ousted from power in 2022, to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad.
However, Tarar said Khan's medical examination was instead conducted at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) "in view of the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside" Shifa International Hospital.
He added that doctors from Shifa International Hospital were present during the medical examination at PIMS.
The Supreme Court had allowed Khan to remain in the hospital until the next hearing of his case on Sept 16.
Khan, a former cricket World Cup-winning captain, has been in jail since August 2023 following convictions in several cases that he and his PTI party have branded politically motivated.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMHE Q2 earnings jump six-fold on heavy engineering boost
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering Holdings Bhd (MMHE) posted a stronger net profit in the second quarter of financial year 2026 (Q2 FY26), driven by a higher contribution from its heavy engineering segment.
Net profit jumped more than six-fold to RM60.59 million from RM10 million a year earlier, while revenue surged 128.6 per cent to RM986.7 million from RM431.57 million.
For the first half of FY26, net profit rose to RM74.9 million from RM22 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 70 per cent to RM1.5 billion from RM884.7 million.
MMHE said the global energy industry outlook remained dynamic amid geopolitical and economic uncertainties, as well as shifting investment priorities.
It said heightened concerns over energy security and supply reliability were influencing capital allocation decisions, with selective investments in upstream developments and energy infrastructure expected to support industry activity and create opportunities for the company.
Against this backdrop, the heavy engineering segment will take a strategic and selective approach to securing a quality order book across conventional and new energy sectors, both domestically and internationally.
This is aimed at maintaining a balanced portfolio while ensuring strong project execution discipline.
Meanwhile, global ship trading, docking and repair operations have been affected by geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East, although long-term marine repair demand is expected to remain resilient, supported by LNG carrier dry-docking requirements and the growing importance of the LNG value chain.
MMHE said it would focus on strengthening its presence in targeted market segments while positioning itself to capitalise on changing regional shipping patterns and emerging market opportunities.
"Yard modernisation efforts are progressing steadily to further enhance productivity, operational efficiency and competitiveness, supporting the company's long-term growth prospects and its ability to deliver value-added solutions to its clients," it added.

Title: Penang tightens short-term rental rules, gives operators 2 month to register
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has introduced new licensing rules for short-term rentals, giving operators a two-month grace period to register before enforcement begins.
The new Private Short-term Accommodation (Local Authorities of Penang) By-laws 2026 came into force on Aug 1, giving local councils clearer powers to regulate short-term accommodation, including Airbnb-type operations.
Those who fail to comply with the by-laws could face a fine of not more than RM2,000, imprisonment of not more than one year, or both.
State Local Government, Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said operators would be given a two-month grace period to apply for licences, after which enforcement action would be taken.
"We give two months as a grace period for operators to make their applications," he told reporters here today.
The new by-laws require private accommodation operators to obtain a licence from the relevant local authority and comply with requirements covering operations, cleanliness, safety, prohibited activities and public nuisance.
The rules also empower local councils to investigate complaints, enter premises and shut down non-compliant premises.
H'ng said the move was necessary as the growing popularity of short-term rentals had created difficulties for local authorities in determining the actual number of operating units.
He said the state expected to obtain more accurate data on the sector after one to two years of licensing, allowing the government to review and improve its regulatory approach.
The rules come amid 388 complaints linked to illegal private accommodation operations between 2020 and March this year — 364 involving the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and 24 involving the Seberang Prai City Council (MBSP).
"For now, we can trace them through Agoda, Airbnb and other online platforms, as well as complaints from neighbours and nearby residents," he added.
H'ng said the complaints included noise and traffic disturbances, social problems, heavier use of shared facilities in strata properties and behaviour deemed inappropriate by local communities.
Under the new rules, private lodging operations are prohibited in government or statutory body premises, healthcare or childcare centres, workers' hostels, private educational institutions, low-cost and low-medium-cost housing, controlled-price homes and People's Housing Projects.
In MBPP's jurisdiction, a separate planning guideline limits permitted zones to general housing, general business and restricted business areas, subject to the relevant local planning framework.
All types of strata residential properties are prohibited from operating as private lodging in MBPP areas.
However, selected commercial properties, including serviced apartments, small office home offices (SOHOs), shophouses and shop offices, may be considered, while landed properties such as detached, semi-detached and terrace houses may also be considered, subject to planning approval for a change of use.
For serviced apartments, H'ng said operators must also comply with the management corporation's (MC) house rules, with the MC having a say in whether short-term rental operations are allowed.
He said MBSP would review its existing procedures and requirements, including whether to designate specific areas suitable for private lodging operations.
The new licensing regime imposes an administrative fee of RM50 per application, while annual licensing fees start at RM1,000 for properties with up to three rooms, with an annual private lodging fee of RM1,800 per unit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six charged with kidnapping Singaporean man for RM63,000 ransom
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU: Six people, including a woman, pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to kidnapping a Singaporean man and demanding RM63,000 in ransom earlier this month.
M. Balamurugam, 46, K. Saravanan, 40, P. Sri Devi, 41, G. Puganeswaran, 38, S. Gobinath, 38, and X. Adwin Nicholas, 41, entered the pleas after the charges were read before Judge Nor Aziati Jaafar.
According to the charge, the six, acting in furtherance of their common intention, kidnapped Al-Shameer Abdul Nassar with the intention of demanding S$20,000 (RM63,000) in ransom.
The offence was allegedly committed in front of a church at No. 22, Jalan Orkid, Skudai, here, at about 2pm on Aug 8.
They were charged under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to 40 years and whipping upon conviction.
Lawyer K. Veeranesh, representing Sri Devi, applied for bail, saying his client was unemployed and had six children aged between 1 and 22.
The other accused, who were unrepresented, also applied for bail, citing their children and family dependants.
In a separate Magistrate's court here, all six also pleaded not guilty before magistrate A. Shaarmini to jointly abducting a Singaporean woman with the intention of causing her to be secretly and wrongfully confined.
They were charged with committing the offence at an apartment in Jalan Aman, Skudai, and several locations around the city about 6.30pm on Aug 11.
The six were charged under Section 365 of the Penal Code, read with Section 34 of the same law, which carries a maximum seven-year jail term and a fine upon conviction.
Meanwhile, in another Sessions Court here, Balamurugam, Saravanan and Gobinath pleaded not guilty before Judge Madihah Zainol to a charge of gang-robbery involving a gold necklace and a Rolex watch belonging to the same victim.
The offence was allegedly committed inside a car in the Johor Bahru Utara area at about 2pm on Aug 8.
They were charged under Section 395 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum 20-year jail term and whipping.
The court granted bail of RM60,000 each to Sri Devi, Adwin Nicholas and Puganeswaran, while Balamurugam, Saravanan and Gobinath were granted bail of RM69,000 each, with local sureties.
The court also ordered them not to interfere with the victims or prosecution witnesses, report to the nearest police station once a month and surrender their passports to the court, if they have them.
The court fixed Sept 23 for mention of the cases and appointment of lawyers.
In a separate magistrate's court, magistrate Nurzihan Abdul Rehman fined Saravanan and Puganeswaran RM3,000 each after they pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to the male victim with a knife.
They were charged with committing the offence at an apartment in Taman Skudai Baru, Skudai, between 10am and 1pm on Aug 11.
The charge was framed under Section 324 of the Penal Code, read with Section 34 of the same law, which provides for a jail term of up to 10 years, a fine or whipping upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutors Nor Deana Aqilah Aliman, R. Nevina and Eizlan Azhar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perak stands firm on vape sales ban despite court challenge
Article:
IPOH: The state government will not back down from its decision to ban the sale of electronic cigarettes, or vapes, despite a legal challenge by a vape association and a company.
State Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the parties had filed a judicial review application against the state government at the Ipoh High Court on March 18.
He said the challenge appeared to question whether the state government had acted beyond the powers or jurisdiction conferred by law.
"That is their right, and the state government has entered an appearance and will file its defence.
"We will not bow to any party trying to prevent the government from taking action to safeguard the people's well-being.
"We will meet them in court, as the state executive council meeting last week decided to proceed with the case, which will be handled by the State Legal Adviser's Office," he said.
Sivanesan said this after launching the "Golden Years Greater Lives" Community Towards Healthy and Dignified Ageing Programme at the Buntong Health Clinic today.
He said the judicial review was filed by the president of the Malaysia E-Vaporizers and Tobacco Alternative Association (MEVTA) and vape company SS City Electronics Enterprise.
He said the state government was named as the first respondent, followed by the Perak menteri besar as the second respondent and the Tanjong Malim District Council as the third respondent.
Sivanesan said the state government's decision was based on the Local Government Act 1976, which empowers local authorities to decide whether to issue business licences for specific purposes.
"It is within the jurisdiction of local authorities. The state government has decided not to allow the sale of vapes at premises under the jurisdiction of local authorities from Jan 1, 2026.
"At the same time, the federal government has also taken steps to amend the relevant laws."
Sivanesan was previously reported as saying that vape operators had been given until
October 2026
to cease sales following the state's decision to stop issuing licences for the sale of vape products in Perak.
The transition period was given to allow affected operators to make the necessary preparations before the ban is fully enforced.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt challenges Duta Enclave land valuation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government today challenged a chartered surveyor's valuation of the Duta Enclave land, saying the rate was too high and unsupported by comparable transactions.
Senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan raised the issue while cross-examining chartered surveyor Foo Gee Jen during the compensation assessment hearing to resolve a long-standing pre-independence land dispute between the government and Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd.
Nurhafizza questioned Foo on several comparable transactions involving bungalow lots in Bukit Tunku, which the witness had used to assess the 1956 market value of the 263.272-acre subject property.
Foo's witness statement says he used the comparison approach and made adjustments to five comparable transactions before arriving at his assessment.
Nurhafizza pointed out that the adjusted values for several of the comparable transactions were below RM6,000 per acre and asked Foo whether he agreed that his adopted rate was therefore high.
Foo disagreed.
He also disagreed with the suggestion that his valuation was unsupported by documentary evidence or the government's valuation reports.
Nurhafizza then focused on the accessibility of the land, asking Foo whether he agreed that the subject property did not have direct access.
Foo disagreed.
However, Foo said he could not recall describing the road he had referred to as a private road and later acknowledged that he was unclear about its status.
Foo's witness statement says the whole original holding had access to Jalan Ipoh through a crossing at the Segambut Railway Halt, with access to the subject property via a secondary road.
He maintained that the acquisition altered the original layout and continuity of the holding, leaving the remaining land without alternative access.
Asked whether secure access to a public road was better than access via a private road, Foo agreed.
He also agreed that Bukit Tunku was a more mature area.
However, Foo maintained that accessibility remained a relevant factor in his assessment.
Nurhafizza also pointed out that Foo's valuation report did not make a separate adjustment for access, to which he agreed.
Foo's evidence is that the subject property had been part of a much larger 700.75-acre holding and that its acquisition severed the original landholding, adversely affecting the development potential and market value of the remaining land.
The witness also maintained that the historical evidence available to him did not conclusively establish the precise physical circumstances of the land in 1956.
His witness statement says he had sought several historical documents, including acquisition plans, revenue survey sheets and official confirmation of the land's zoning and development density as at 1956, but had not been provided with them.
Foo also disputed the reliability of two undated Revenue Survey Sheets, saying they showed infrastructure including Jalan Duta and the New Klang Valley Expressway that was only built decades after 1956.
Semantan's legal battle began in 2003 when it sued the government, claiming the 106ha parcel in the city was unlawfully acquired in 1956.
The disputed land houses several major government complexes, including the Inland Revenue Board headquarters, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Academy, the National Archives and the Kuala Lumpur Syariah Court complex.
In 2009, the High Court ruled in Semantan's favour, but subsequent appellate decisions held that the company was not entitled to the land title.
On June 24 last year, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan was instead entitled to adequate compensation based on the land's value in 1956, and ordered an assessment of mesne profits.
On Nov 13 the same year, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan's application for leave to appeal, leaving the Court of Appeal's decision intact and paving the way for the current assessment proceedings.
The hearing before High Court judge Roslan Mat Nor continues on Sept 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Operational excellence key to Asean's energy transition – TNB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Operational excellence must go beyond cost efficiency to strengthen grid resilience, enhance real-time system visibility and support the safe and reliable integration of renewable energy as Asean's energy landscape continues to evolve.
Speaking at the 3rd Asean Operational Excellence Summit 2026 (OPEX 2026), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) chief strategy and ventures officer Dr Mohd Fadzil Mohd Siamhe said the increasing interconnection of power systems and accelerating energy transition require utilities to build greater agility in responding to a rapidly changing operating environment.
"Operational excellence must go beyond cost efficiency. It is about strengthening grid resilience, enhancing real-time system visibility, integrating renewable energy safely and reliably, and building the agility to respond effectively to an increasingly dynamic operating environment," he said.
For TNB, he said transformation is driven by the integration of data, digital technologies and advanced analytics into everyday grid operations.
"Continued investments in network modernisation, predictive asset management and enhanced incident response capabilities enable TNB to improve reliability, minimise service disruptions and deliver secure, resilient electricity supply to the communities and economies it serves," he said.
Equally important is investing in people, he said, adding that while technology is a key enabler, operational excellence ultimately depends on a skilled and future-ready workforce.
"TNB continues to strengthen technical capabilities through continuous upskilling, digital enablement and a strong culture of safety, innovation and continuous improvement."
Mohd Fadzil also underscored that Asean's energy future will be shaped not only by technological advancement, but by stronger regional collaboration.
"Through knowledge sharing, operational benchmarking and deeper partnerships among Asean utilities, TNB remains committed to advancing a more resilient, sustainable and interconnected regional power system that supports long-term energy security and shared prosperity."
The third OPEX 2026, held in Kuala Lumpur recently, brought together regional utilities and industry leaders to exchange insights and best practices on strengthening operational performance amid the region's rapidly changing energy landscape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Velesto profit drops in Q2, but says outlook brightens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Velesto Energy Bhd's net profit dropped 98.9 per cent in the second quarter, but the oil and gas services group expects its performance to strengthen in the coming quarters.
Velesto's net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 fell to RM531,000 from RM50.44 million a year earlier, mainly due to lower rig utilisation and daily charter rates.
Velesto president Megat Zariman Abdul Rahim said the company's performance is expected to strengthen in the coming quarters, supported by contracted activity and a sizeable pipeline of prospects.
"Five of our six rigs are contracted until end-2026, with a healthy RM1.3 billion remaining order book and RM3.7 billion in prospects as at July 2026," he said in a statement.
Velesto said its drilling services segment recorded a lower revenue of RM149.5 million for the current quarter, compared to RM195.8 million a year ago.
This was mainly due to lower average daily charter rates of US$103,000 per day, compared to US$123,000 in the corresponding quarter.
For the cumulative six months, the company's earnings dropped 72.5 per cent YoY to RM28.39 million from RM103.04 million last year while revenue dropped to 337.38 million from RM424.56 million.
Meanwhile, Velesto said its rigs achieved 99.9 per cent uptime, while advancing its asset-light growth strategy through securing the Hibiscus contract via a third-party rig and the Chevron i-RDC 2.0 contract for Naga 8.
"We also continue to actively pursue opportunities for Naga 3. With sustained focus on energy security, we see continued demand for jack-up drilling services in Malaysia and across Southeast Asia," he said.
Velesto declared a second interim dividend of 0.25 sen per share, bringing the year-to-date dividend to 1.0 sen per share.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Filipino woman jailed 5 months for MyKad offence
Article:
KUANTAN: A 45-year-old Filipino woman was sentenced to five months in prison after pleading guilty to using another person's details to apply for a replacement MyKad.
Lorna Adilun was sentenced by magistrate Ellyna Othman at the magistrate's court here today. The sentence was ordered to run from the date of her arrest.
The shop assistant was charged with deliberately providing false information when applying for a replacement identity card under the identity of another person at the National Registration Department (NRD) branch at the Pahang Urban Transformation Centre at 4.19pm on June 9.
According to the case facts, Lorna used the identity of a person known as Zuriah when applying for the replacement MyKad. She was issued a payment receipt and a temporary identification document.
Checks by the NRD's identity card unit in Putrajaya found that her fingerprints did not match those of the registered holder of the identity.
Lorna was detained on Aug 18 when she returned to the UTC to collect the MyKad.
Further checks found that she had never been issued an identity card and that the MyKad number she had provided belonged to Zuriah. She was also found to be an undocumented immigrant from the Philippines.
Lorna was charged under Regulation 25(1)(b) of the National Registration Regulations 1990, which provides for a jail term of up to three years, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both upon conviction.
The prosecution was handled by Pahang NRD prosecuting officers Fahkrol Anuar Sani and Mohd Nurhisyam Mohd Sofian, while Lorna was unrepresented.
In mitigation, Lorna told the court that she worked at a food stall and lived with her employer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family seeks answers over Kepong petrol attack after suspect's arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The family of a woman who suffered burns to about 50 per cent of her body in a petrol attack in Kepong is seeking answers about her relationship with the suspect.
The victim's daughter, Yap, said the family was relieved following the suspect's arrest but remained frustrated that they had yet to receive an official explanation from police about what led to the attack.
Police have said the incident was believed to have stemmed from a personal grudge.
"Personally, a heavy weight has been lifted off my chest. Now that he is caught, we can fully focus our energy on my mother's recovery.
"But we still deserve to know the real reason why he did this to her," she told the New Straits Times.
Yap, who is the fourth of five siblings in a single-parent family, said the family was particularly concerned about police describing the 59-year-old suspect and her 62-year-old mother as acquaintances.
"At this point, we're still waiting for confirmation from the police. So far, we've only seen police reports and articles saying the suspect claimed that they knew each other or that there was a personal grudge.
"But what exactly does 'acquaintance' mean? Were they friends? Was it simply a business or customer relationship? Did the police find any contact between them on my mother's phone?
"We don't know, because the family has not received any further updates from the police. So we're still waiting for them to clarify what their relationship actually was," she said.
Yap said her mother remained in the intensive care unit (ICU) in an unstable condition, sedated and intubated.
She underwent her fourth surgery yesterday after the procedure was postponed due to her fragile condition.
Yap said the family remained hopeful for her recovery while waiting for further updates from police.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect knew the victim, although the pair were not believed to have been close.
He said the suspect was believed to have been unhappy with the victim over a matter involving lottery numbers, with police now investigating whether other factors were involved.
"Our investigations so far indicate that the incident stemmed from a personal grudge. Cases like this are very rare. Setting someone on fire is an extreme act of violence," he said at a press conference at the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters.
The suspect was
arrested
at his home in Kepong on Tuesday (Aug 18), more than a week after the Aug 9 attack. He was also believed to have suffered burns to his hands during the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar military offensive targets land for Russia-backed port project
Article:
MYANMAR'S military has deployed hundreds of troops to forcibly clear areas marked for a Russia-backed special economic zone in the country's south, burning villages and sealing off surrounding tracts of land, according to resistance fighters and a local activist with direct knowledge.
The offensive around the Dawei Special Economic Zone (SEZ) — that includes a planned deep-sea port and power plant on the Andaman Sea — is the clearest sign yet that Myanmar's military-backed government is willing to use force to revive a project touted as a strategic alternative to the Strait of Malacca. The push also coincides with a diplomatic charm offensive: junta chief-turned-President Min Aung Hlaing pitched Dawei as a potential gateway to South and West Asia during a landmark visit to Thailand this month and discussed the project again this week in talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
Since July, the military has pumped hundreds of soldiers into the southern Tanintharyi Region, bordering Thailand, where Dawei is located, sparking battles with local resistance groups who have been forced to retreat, according to two sources.
"The military is advancing its columns and conducting area-clearance operations. Some villages and homes have been burned down," Saw Dah Ko of the Tanintharyi Region People's Defence Force told Reuters. A second resistance fighter from the Dawei District No.1 battalion operating under the shadow National Unity Government, said troops had torched houses in at least three villages and killed three aid workers who were supporting displaced communities.
"They want to run this Dawei SEZ, so they want to clear the area here," the second fighter said, referring to the military and asking not to be named.
The three aid workers were detained and killed after encountering an advancing military column in Yebyu Township on July 9, local civil society group MAGGA Initiative said in a statement.
Reuters could not independently verify the accounts, and the Myanmar government and Russia's embassy in Myanmar did not respond to requests for comment.
FREQUENT SKIRMISHES
The intensification followed a late-June visit to southern Myanmar by armed forces' deputy chief Kyaw Swar Lin, who urged soldiers to protect "strategic projects" such as Dawei.
"Since then, a column of approximately 700 soldiers has been advancing into relevant surrounding areas, raiding villages and killing civilians," conflict monitor ACLED said in an August report.
The offensive around the Dawei SEZ has been reinforced by air and naval attacks, overwhelming loosely organised local resistance groups, according to Saw Dah Ko and a local activist.
"They enter the region, and once reinforced by the navy, they launch offensives into the villages situated within the deep sea port project area," said Min Lwin Oo of the Democracy Movement Strike Committee, referring to the military.
"When they launch these offensives, skirmishes occur frequently." The Dawei push reflects a broader strategy by the military to reclaim strategic territory and border zones it lost to opposition groups since a 2021 coup, which triggered a civil war that has killed some 100,000 people and displaced over 3.5 million. The military engineered a widely criticsed election in December and January, with no substantial opposition allowed to run, clearing the way for Min Aung Hlaing to become president.
ALTERNATE TO MALACCA STRAIT
Originally launched in 2008 as a joint venture with Thailand, the project aimed to facilitate trade between Southeast Asian countries and West and East Asia. But work on the Dawei SEZ stalled in 2013 due to local opposition and funding shortages. In January 2021, just weeks before the coup, the committee overseeing the SEZ said it had moved to terminate 2015-2016 agreements for nine projects in the initial construction phase.
"We will now focus our efforts on finding new partners to unlock the potential of the Dawei Special Economic Zone," the committee's chairman said in a statement.
Myanmar's new government is now looking to revive the project with the support of Russia, a key ally for Min Aung Hlaing and the military.
At a business forum in Moscow on Wednesday, Tanintharyi Region Chief Minister Zaw Naing Oo said that the project could enable cargo to move four to six days quicker than if it were to traverse the Strait of Malacca.
State media reported that he also touted the port's proximity — about 45 km (28 miles) — to Myanmar's major offshore gas fields.
Russian companies intend to work with Dawei SEZ, aiming to expand trade and create new jobs, including in small and medium businesses, Russia's Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said this week in a meeting with Min Aung Hlaing.
The project could give Russia greater market access in Southeast Asia and a port footprint in the Indian Ocean region, according to a source with knowledge of Moscow's thinking, who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter.
"The risk in Myanmar is still very high," the source said, "Russian investments will have to be linked to connectivity with Thailand for the project to make sense."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pig farm in Perak told to halt expansion works pending approval
Article:
IPOH: A pig farm operator in Kampung Perlop 1, Sungai Siput, has been told to stop expansion works after carrying out land levelling while its application for planning permission is still being processed.
State Human Resources, Health, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the operator had breached procedures by carrying out construction-related works before obtaining approval from the local authority.
He said the farm was in the process of being converted from a conventional operation into a modern, fully enclosed pig farming facility.
"We have instructed the local authority and District and Land Office to take action.
"Although the farm has applied for planning permission and the application is being processed, it cannot carry out any construction works until approval is obtained," he said.
He told reporters this after launching the "Golden Years Greater Lives" Community Programme Towards Healthy and Dignified Ageing at Buntong Health Clinic here today.
Sivanesan was responding to concerns raised by Sungai Siput Umno Youth chief Ariff Zaky Zolkafly on Facebook, questioning whether the farm's expansion had obtained the necessary approvals following complaints from residents about a fly nuisance.
Sivanesan said an inspection found that the land works involved the construction of five new sewage retention ponds.
"One of the four existing sewage retention ponds was also found to be discharging water through a pipe directly into a tributary.
"Water samples have been taken for Biochemical Oxygen Demand analysis and sent to a laboratory in Bukit Tengah, Penang, for further testing," he said.
He said authorities were also investigating the level of fly infestation at the farm.
Meanwhile, he said the state government expected that modernising the pig farming industry could generate up to RM1.6 billion in state revenue, including through the leasing of 174ha of state land used for pig farming.
"If all 85 pig farms in Perak are taken into account, the state could potentially collect almost RM1.6 billion, including revenue from the 174 hectares of state-owned land used by pig farmers.
"Currently, what we receive from pig farming is only about RM300,000 through licences issued by the DVS," he said.
He said Perak remained the country's largest pig farming state, although the number of farms had declined to 85 due to closures and consolidation among operators.
He said the restructuring of the industry was also aimed at ensuring all pig farms adopted a fully enclosed system, with full enforcement scheduled to begin on Jan 1, 2027.
"There will be no compromise in the conversion from conventional to modern pig farms. They must convert their farms or face closure," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says Felda task force has begun work
Article:
BANGI: A special task force investigating issues involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) has begun its work, with its findings expected to be announced once the investigations are completed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the task force would conduct a broad review covering past problems, improvements to management and measures needed to strengthen Felda moving forward.
"The special task force has started its work. I am waiting for the investigation to be completed before we announce the findings in the near future," he told reporters after a session with Felda leadership and management here today.
Asked about the scope of the task force, Anwar said it would examine all relevant aspects, including previous shortcomings as well as Felda's current management and future direction.
"Everything, including improving management and identifying past problems. But what is important is the current management and the steps moving forward," he added.
On Saturday, Anwar said the government would uncover alleged governance failures within Felda, which has been saddled with substantial debt.
He said the move was not intended to prejudge or punish anyone, but to establish the facts and ensure that any wrongdoing was properly investigated.
Anwar said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had also called for investigations into governance failures to extend beyond Lembaga Tabung Haji.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gambling, traffic and permit issues raise concerns in Bukit Bintang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Illegal gambling, traffic congestion and foreigners working or operating businesses without valid permits are among the main complaints in Bukit Bintang, prompting calls for more "drastic" enforcement.
Keadilan Bukit Bintang Public Complaints Bureau chairman Tengku Imran Tengku Zainal Abidin said these issues were tarnishing the image of the capital's premier tourism and commercial hub.
He said the presence of premises suspected of operating online gambling activities had become a major concern for the local community.
"This matter needs to be thoroughly investigated.
"If there are elements of wrongdoing, enforcement action must be taken immediately under existing laws," he said in a statement to Harian Metro.
He also said the district's traffic flow was being crippled by illegal parking, double parking and vehicles obstructing pedestrian walkways.
"We do not want Bukit Bintang to be known only as a business hub while simultaneously facing safety and comfort issues.
"Constant and sustained enforcement is vital in these high-traffic areas."
The bureau reported a spike in complaints regarding foreigners operating businesses or working without valid permits.
He urged the Immigration Department and related agencies to conduct integrated operations to ensure legal compliance, regardless of the individuals' backgrounds.
The statement also addressed the growing nuisance of aggressive beggars in tourist-heavy zones.
"This is not just an enforcement issue; it involves elements of human exploitation and public safety. Action must involve both enforcement and welfare agencies," he said.
To bolster security, the bureau proposed the establishment of a permanent police post or increased patrols in high-density spots such as Jalan Alor, particularly at night.
"It is time for the city's key commercial artery to reflect a safe and comfortable image.
"Integrated enforcement will ensure the local community feels at ease and ensure Bukit Bintang remains a top destination for both locals and international tourists," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Genting shares fall 6pct after Q2 earnings miss expectations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd's share price fell nearly six per cent after its second-quarter (Q2) earnings fell short of analysts' expectations.
The stock dropped 13 sen or 5.8 per cent to RM2.11 per share with more than 9.38 million shares changing hands. This valued the company at about RM8.18 billion.
Year-to-date, Genting's shares have fallen 87 sen, or 29.2 per cent, from RM2.98.
Meanwhile, its 74 per cent-owned unit Genting Malaysia Bhd saw its shares slip three sen or 1.7 per cent to RM1.70 per share after reporting a near 90 per cent decline in Q2 net profit to RM47.4 million in Q2 from RM416.6 million in the same period last year.
Genting posted a net loss of RM27 million from RM243.5 million last year, despite revenue rising to RM7.75 billion from RM6.78 billion.
The company attributed the weaker bottom line mainly to foreign exchange translation losses, as well as higher finance and operating costs.
Public Investment Bank Bhd analyst Eltricia Foong said the performances of both Genting and Genting Malaysia came in well below expectations.
This prompted the firm to cut its earnings forecasts for Genting and Genting Malaysia for financial years 2026 to 2028 (FY26-28) by an average of 18 per cent and 11 per cent respectively.
"The operating environment for the entertainment and hospitality industry remains challenging amid rising geopolitical tensions that restrict travel demand and increase operating costs," she said in a note.
PublicInvest maintained a "Neutral" call on both stocks with a target price of RM2.35 for Genting and RM1.73 for Genting Malaysia.
Foong said while earnings are expected to recover gradually, visibility remains weak as geopolitical tensions and slower economic activity could weigh on the global hospitality and entertainment industry.
She expects operating costs to rise in the second half of FY26 due to higher energy costs.
"We do not expect the US operations to deliver higher earnings in the immediate term, in view of the weakening job market and consumer confidence," she said.
Foong also raised concerns over Genting's gearing level given the heavy capital commitments of its subsidiaries, Genting Malaysia and Genting Singapore, for their development projects at Resorts World New York City and Resorts World Sentosa.
On Genting Malaysia, she said the full-scale expansion of its New York casino could eventually act as a catalyst, but was unlikely to be earnings-accretive over the next one to two years given its hefty US$5.5 billion project cost.
Resorts World New York City launched its first table games on April 28, ahead of its competitors, which could help boost gross gaming revenue.
However, Foong expects operating costs to rise amid inflationary pressures in the US.
She also cautioned that continued de-dollarisation could erode the value of the company's US dollar investments over time if future gross gaming revenue fails to match historical growth rates.
She added that changing consumer preferences, particularly younger consumers' increasing preference for online gaming platforms over traditional physical casinos, could affect Genting Malaysia's long-term growth prospects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar seeks Prabowo's help over Felda Eagle High investment
Article:
BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has written to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto seeking his assistance in looking into issues surrounding the Federal Land Development Authority's (Felda) investment in Eagle High Plantations.
Anwar cited the investment as an example of past decisions involving Felda that had resulted in billions of ringgit in losses, stressing that such failures should not be allowed to recur.
"I have written to President Prabowo asking him to also look into this matter. If it is not addressed, the losses would amount to RM2.5 billion, while what we may eventually recover is RM200 million. This is one example," he said during an engagement session with Felda's top management and managers here today.
Present was Felda director-general Datuk Dr Suzana Idayu Wati Osman.
Anwar said Felda managers needed to understand the scale of the problems inherited by the agency and how poor decisions at the top could ultimately affect the organisation as a whole.
"I want the managers to know about these problems and how heavy the burden becomes when there is mismanagement.
"What does a Felda manager in Pahang, Johor or Kedah have to do with it? We all have to bear the consequences. That is the problem," he said.
Anwar said issues involving investigations, enforcement action and court proceedings should be left to the relevant authorities, but stressed that Felda's management must learn from previous failures.
He said proper governance must remain a priority throughout Felda, rejecting attempts to trivialise questions over accountability and past losses.
"I have told Suzana that I want the managers to understand all these problems so that we do not assume everything is fine, or dismiss them as minor matters," he added.
Felda, through its subsidiary FIC Properties Sdn Bhd (FICP),
signed a deal with Indonesia's Rajawali Group
to acquire a 37 per cent stake in Eagle High Plantations for US$505.4 million, or about RM2.3 billion, in 2016.
The deal included a put option allowing FICP to sell the stake back to Rajawali if certain conditions were not fulfilled. Felda subsequently sought to exercise the option, leading to arbitration proceedings at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC).
In June 2024, the
arbitration tribunal ruled in FICP's favour
and directed Rajawali to repurchase the Eagle High shares at the agreed price or rate. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Felda had not recorded any profit or dividend earnings from the investment.
However, in a written parliamentary reply to Putrajaya MP Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin in August last year,
Zahid said Felda had yet to enforce the award
after Rajawali filed a petition at the Central Jakarta District Court seeking to annul or block its enforcement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kossan earnings forecast trimmed amid higher costs, falling prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts have cut their target prices for Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd after revising down their earnings forecasts for the glovemaker.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) lowered its target price to RM1.13 from RM1.24 while maintaining its "Hold" recommendation.
CIMB Securities cut its target to RM1.19 from RM1.26, also retaining its "Hold" call.
HLIB lowered its financial year 2026 (FY26) earnings forecast by 11.0 per cent.
This is mainly to account for a sharp contraction in the third quarter (Q3) FY26 pre-tax profit margin, as higher-cost inventories flow through production amid declining average selling prices (ASPs).
"We have also lowered our Q4 FY26 pre-tax margin assumption, factoring in a potential 40 per cent increase in natural gas prices.
"For FY27/FY28, we cut our forecasts by 13.0 per cent and 8.4 per cent, respectively, to incorporate more conservative ASPs and sales volume assumptions amid persistent structural oversupply in the generic medical rubber glove segment," HLIB said in a note.
The firm said Kossan's glove and clean-room segment is expected to post weaker quarter-on-quarter earnings in Q3 FY26.
It said the weaker performance would be driven by a significant contraction in margins as higher-cost inventories are used in production, alongside declining ASPs from their peak in May 2026.
HLIB expects the company's technical rubber products segment to operate in a mixed market environment, with demand from the infrastructure sector continuing its gradual recovery.
The automotive segment is likely to remain subdued amid global trade uncertainties and persistent cost pressures.
"Overall, we expect group earnings to deteriorate materially in Q3 FY26 due to the glove & clean-room segment," HLIB said.
CIMB Securities said Kossan's first-half (1H26) core net profit stood at RM105 million, accounting for 60 per cent of its full-year forecast and 65 per cent of consensus estimates.
"We deem the results to be in line, given our expectation of sequentially weaker 2H26 earnings following the windfall ASPs achieved in 1H26," it said.
The firm cut its calendar year 2026 (CY26) core net profit (CNP) forecast by six per cent, mainly due to a lower ASPs assumption and higher cost assumptions.
"However, we leave our CY27 and CY28 estimates unchanged.
"Following the earnings revision, we have reduced our target price to RM1.19, from RM1.26, based on an unchanged CY27 price to book ratio of 0.8 times, to reflect a weaker profitability outlook," it said.

Title: Police escorts should protect, not privilege, says criminologist
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police escorts and emergency signals for VIPs must be based on necessity and public interest, not status, says senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy.
His comments come after a father and his two daughters were killed when they were struck by an
Immigration Department truck
at the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection in Kuala Lumpur.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said flashing beacon lights and sirens did not give enforcement or emergency vehicle drivers carte blanche to
run red lights
.
He said drivers must first ensure an intersection was clear and safe before proceeding through a red light.
Sundramoorthy said the use of police escorts, sirens and strobe lights for eminent individuals should be governed by clear criteria to preserve equality before the law and public trust in policing.
"Rank should not become a traffic privilege," he told the New Straits Times, stressing that protection and traffic priority were not the same.
He said there was a strong case for appropriate protection for the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Malay Rulers, Governors, Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Menteri Besars, as well as visiting foreign Heads of State, where security assessments justified such measures.
[[nid:1515860]]
However, he said sirens and emergency lights should be proportionate to the assessed threat, even for such dignitaries.
"Rank alone should not create an automatic entitlement to emergency traffic privileges," he said.
Sundramoorthy said the Inspector-General and Deputy Inspector-General of Police could also face legitimate security risks arising from their responsibilities, but police directors, state police chiefs and other senior officers should not automatically receive sirens and strobe lights because of their rank.
He said emergency signals used by the Fire and Rescue Department should similarly be reserved for genuine emergencies, including fires, road crashes, rescue operations, hazardous-material incidents and major disasters.
"The justification is the urgency of the emergency, not the status of personnel," he added.
Sundramoorthy called for the authorities to establish a clear policy specifying who could receive an escort, who could authorise it, when emergency signals could be activated and what constituted genuine necessity.
He said every use of such privileges should be documented and periodically audited.
"Malaysia does not need to eliminate police escorts; it needs to eliminate ambiguity," he said.
