Title: Muhyiddin trial: Witness says MOF wanted open tender, but PMO insisted on pre-qualification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) had initially wanted government projects under the Bumiputera contractors' programme Jana Wibawa to be carried out through open tender, but the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) had instructed for Jana Wibawa projects to be given out either by direct negotiation or through a pre-qualification tender, a senior MOF officer said today.
Datin Rosni Mohd Yusoff, who heads the Finance Ministry's government procurement division as its Under Secretary, said this as the 25th prosecution witness in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's power abuse and money laundering trial.
At the time of the Jana Wibawa programme during Muhyiddin's administration, Rosni was the deputy under secretary of the same division and also chaired a Finance Ministry committee that evaluated whether proposed contractors forwarded by the PMO were qualified to be given Jana Wibawa projects.
Today, Rosni explained why she had told the High Court that the prime minister has no power under the law and government procurement rules to order for a project to be awarded through direct negotiation to any specific company.
"Because the instruction that we received from PMO to carry out this project is through the Finance Minister's office. The Finance Minister instructed the procurement division to carry out evaluation.
"Initially, Jana Wibawa, we wanted to carry out through open tender, but we received instructions from PMO. The decision to determine the project through direct negotiation and pre-qualification came from PMO," she told the High Court.
In other words, Rosni said the PMO was deciding on which Jana Wibawa projects should be given out through direct negotiation or pre-qualification tender.
Rosni had previously said that it is actually the finance minister who has the power under government procurement rules to decide whether a project should be carried out through direct negotiation or pre-qualification tender.
Direct negotiation means that only a single contractor is considered for a project without competition from other contractors on factors such as prices, while pre-qualification tender is a form of limited tender where only pre-screened companies with the required experience, financial and technical capabilities are allowed to bid for a project.
What role did PMO play in government's procurement for these three Jana Wibawa projects?
In the Jana Wibawa programme, the PMO on November 13, 2020 gave a list of 54 proposed contractors for the Finance Ministry to evaluate for appointment as contractors for 54 projects through direct negotiation.
One of the 54 proposed contractors was KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, which initially failed an evaluation by Rosni's committee as it had a record of sick projects, before passing a second round of evaluation by the same committee due to additional information provided by the PMO on KCJ Engineering.
KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd was later appointed as a contractor through direct negotiation for the RM62 million Jana Wibawa project to build a new road connecting Felda Bukit Jalor to Gemas, Negeri Sembilan.
Separately, the PMO had also in early 2021 forwarded several companies' names including Sutracom Sdn Bhd and Nepturis Sdn Bhd to the Finance Ministry for evaluation to join in pre-qualification tenders for two separate Jana Wibawa projects.
Under the pre-qualification tender method, Sutracom later won a RM605.2 million project to build and upgrade phase three of the Pulau Indah highway in Klang, Selangor, while Nepturis won a RM141 million contract to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD).
Today, Rosni confirmed that the PMO did not interfere in her committee's evaluation of these three contractors for the three Jana Wibawa projects, but stressed that the Finance Ministry's direction to her to evaluate was ultimately due to an instruction originating from the PM's office.
Rosni explained that PMO instructed the finance minister to evaluate these proposed Jana Wibawa contractors, and that the instruction then flowed down the hierarchy from the Finance Minister's office to her division's Under Secretary, and from the Under Secretary to her as the Deputy Under Secretary.
"When the decision was made, that decision did not have interference from PMO. But the instruction to evaluate these companies is from the PMO through the Finance Minister," Rosni told deputy public prosecutor Noralis Mat.
Explaining that this is the process in the civil service, Rosni agreed with Noralis that the Finance Ministry's instruction to her to evaluate these companies as potential Jana Wibawa contractors would not have come out of the blue.
Rosni said she had received instructions from her then superior, then Under Secretary Datuk Zamzuri Abdul Aziz, that MOF would process or evaluate companies' applications for Jana Wibawa projects that were forwarded by the PMO.
"I received instructions as Datuk Zamzuri informed to me, where he received instructions from higher-ups, for Jana Wibawa, we only process applications that come from PMO," she said.
Previously, Rosni said her committee at the Finance Ministry would not have evaluated KCJ Engineering, Sutracom and Nepturis if their names were not stated in the prime minister's letters to the Finance Ministry, as evaluations were only carried out on companies proposed by the PMO for Jana Wibawa projects.
PMO was not in MOF's evaluation meetings on Jana Wibawa contractors, but was updated of outcomes
Earlier, during cross-examination by Muhyiddin's lawyer Chetan Jethwani, Rosni confirmed that there were no representatives from the PMO in her committee's four meetings to evaluate KCJ Engineering, Sutracom and Nepturis and that this was intentional as the PMO is not supposed to be present.
Rosni confirmed to Chetan that the PM and the PMO were not involved in the decision-making at these four meetings, and there had been no attempt to interfere with the outcome of that decision-making and also no complaints of such attempts.
Rosni said there was no direct request from the PM or the PMO to her to ask about the outcome of the MOF meetings to evaluate the contractors.
But Rosni said that her committee's evaluation decision was notified to the Public Works Department (JKR) in letters that were copied to the PMO, adding that she had received instructions from her superior Zamzuri that the PMO had instructed for the decision to be copied to them.
Earlier, Rosni agreed with Muhyiddin's lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad that contractors must go through her committee's evaluation for Jana Wibawa projects regardless of whether the project is via direct negotiation or pre-qualification tender.
Rosni agreed that this means that companies are not guaranteed to get the projects even if they were proposed to be appointed via direct negotiation, and agreed that KCJ Engineering's failure in the initial evaluation confirms this fact.
She agreed that the PMO gave additional information on KCJ Engineering because it received a request for additional information from the Finance Minister's then senior private secretary Datuk Wan Murtadza Wan Mahmud.
Among other things, Rosni told Amer that her committee checks potential Jana Wibawa contractors' beneficial ownership based on the Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM)'s records and the Construction Industry Development Board's (CIDB) Centralized Information Management System (CIMS).
Rosni agreed that her committee would not be able to obtain such information if the companies did not declare their beneficial ownership to SSM or CIDB.
Rosni agreed with Amer's suggestion that the objective was to ensure that no "Ali Baba" companies would get Jana Wibawa projects and to ensure that Bumiputera companies are genuinely controlled by Bumiputera as registered.
Previously, evidence and testimonies from prosecution witnesses showed that Bersatu had received money in its bank accounts from companies that had won Jana Wibawa projects, namely RM800,000 from KCJ Engineering and RM1 million from Nepturis.
Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin had previously also testified that his company donated RM19.5 million to Bersatu as his younger brother’s company Sutracom was awarded the RM605.2 million project.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes on Aug 26.

Title: Afternoon checks show nine Sarawak areas with unhealthy air quality, Serian still very unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Air Pollution Index (API) reading at Serian station in Sarawak reached 227 (very unhealthy) as of 2pm today, while nine other areas in the state recorded unhealthy readings.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said Sri Aman recorded the second-highest API reading at 187, followed by Kuching (176), Samarahan (175), Sarikei (174), Sibu (157), Bintulu and Samalaju (154), as well as Kapit and Mukah (130).
She said air quality nationwide had deteriorated today, with an increase in areas recording unhealthy API readings in Sarawak due to haze moving in from various directions.
Based on a report by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) on August 20, a total of 288 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 53 in Sumatra and two in Malaysia, with one each in Sarawak and Terengganu.
She said the Regional Haze Map issued by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) today showed continued dry weather conditions across most parts of the southern Asean region, except for northeastern Borneo and northern Sumatra, which experienced rainfall.
“Hotspots were detected extensively in Kalimantan, while several isolated hotspots were detected in other parts of the southern Asean region.
“Moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes were observed in West Kalimantan and moving northwards into western Sarawak,” she said in a statement today, adding that the DOE had stepped up enforcement efforts and daily patrols in areas with potential for open burning, in addition to monitoring API readings.
“The National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan have been activated to coordinate action among government agencies in addressing open burning and dealing with the national haze situation,” she said.
The public is advised not to engage in open burning and to report any incidents of open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia at 999, or to the DOE at 1-800-88-2727. — Bernama

Title: MOH bans three batches of Chomel hand sanitiser over excessive methanol content
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has banned the sale of Chomel Hand Sanitizer after three batches of the product were found to contain methanol above the permitted limit.
It said the action was taken by the director of Pharmaceutical Services following tests conducted by the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) on the products under its market surveillance programme for the quality of notified cosmetic products.
According to the MOH, the test results found that the affected product batches did not comply with the specifications stipulated under the Guidelines for Control of Cosmetic Products in Malaysia
“The affected product batches are BN111025, BN01026 and BN061225,” it said in a statement today.
As such, the MOH urged the public not to purchase or use products from the affected batches.
The MOH said methanol is a chemical that is not permitted for use as an active ingredient in cosmetics, including hand sanitisers, except in very small quantities for specific purposes, adding that uncontrolled use may pose serious health risks.
“Uncontrolled exposure to methanol can pose serious health risks. Exposure to methanol through the skin can cause skin and eye irritation, headaches, dizziness, nausea, nervous system damage and visual impairment, including blindness.
“Excessive exposure to methanol or accidental ingestion can result in coma and death,” it added.
As such, the MOH has instructed sellers and distributors to immediately stop the sale and distribution of the affected products, as selling or distributing them constitutes a violation of the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984.
It said individuals found guilty of offences under the regulations may be fined up to RM25,000 or imprisoned for up to three years, or both, for a first offence, and fined up to RM50,000 or imprisoned for up to five years, or both, for subsequent offences.
Companies, meanwhile, can be fined up to RM50,000 for a first offence and up to RM100,000 for subsequent offences.
The MOH also advised the public to immediately stop using the product and seek medical attention if they experience discomfort or adverse reactions. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest drug suspect after struggle with machete leaves officer injured in Jeli
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 21 — A suspect believed to be involved in drug trafficking was arrested after brandishing a machete at police officers and injuring one during a raid in Kampung Lubok Bongor, Jeli, yesterday.
Jeli police chief Supt Kamarulzaman Harun said the 11am incident took place when a team from the district police Criminal Investigation Division raided an unnumbered house in the village.
“The suspect acted aggressively by pulling out a machete tucked at his waist and brandishing it at the police officers while threatening to kill.
“When officers tried to apprehend him, a struggle ensued, and one officer sustained injuries to his left middle finger and left shoulder,” he said in a statement today.
Kamarulzaman said the suspect was arrested and the situation was brought under control without further injuries.
He added that police seized a machete about 36 centimetres long and a transparent plastic packet containing six reddish pills suspected to be yaba.
“The pills were found inside a black waist bag,” he said.
He said preliminary investigations revealed the suspect was wanted by the district Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division for allegedly distributing drugs.
“The suspect was also wanted in connection with an August 19 incident where he threatened to kill while brandishing a machete during a police raid.
“The case is being investigated under Section 324 and Section 353 of the Penal Code, as well as Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952,” he said.
Kamarulzaman added the suspect would be remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to assist further investigations.
He stressed that police would not tolerate any acts of threatening, attacking, or using force against public servants while they perform their duties. — Bernama

Title: Six charged with kidnapping Singaporean man for S$20,000 ransom in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 21 — Six individuals including a woman pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of kidnapping a Singaporean man, 32, for the purpose of obtaining a ransom of S$20,000 (RM63,000), earlier this month.
M. Balamurugan, 46, K. Saravanan, 40, P. Sri Devi, 41, G. Puganeswaran, 38, S. Gobinath, 38, and X. Adwin Nicholas, 41, made the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Nor Aziati Jaafar.
According to the charge, they were charged with the joint intent of kidnapping the victim for the purpose of obtaining the ransom in front of a church in Skudai, at about 2 pm, on Aug 8.
The charges were brought under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961 and read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for a prison sentence of up to 40 years and whipping, if convicted.
Deputy Public Prosecutor R. Nevina did not offer bail on the grounds that the offence was serious and non-bailable.
However, lawyer K. Veeranesh, representing Sri Devi, applied for bail on the grounds that his client was unemployed and had children aged between one and 22, while the other accused also applied for bail on the grounds that they had family responsibilities.
The court then allowed all the accused to be bailed at RM50,000 each with two local sureties, in addition to setting conditions so that they would not harass the victim and prosecution witnesses, report to the nearest police station once a month and surrender their international passports to the court if they had any.
At the Magistrate’s Court, all six accused also pleaded not guilty before Magistrate A. Shaarmini to a charge of kidnapping a Singaporean woman, 33, with the intention of causing the victim to be secretly and wrongfully confined.
They were charged with committing the act at the Skudai Villa Apartment, Jalan Aman, Taman Skudai Baru between 2 pm on Aug 8 and 6.30 pm on Aug 11.
The charge was brought under Section 365 of the Penal Code and read together with Section 34 of the same code which provides for a maximum prison sentence of seven years and a fine, if convicted.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Eizlan Azhar did not offer bail but Veeranesh, who represented Sri Devi, applied for bail.
A. Shaarmini allowed all the accused to be granted bail of RM10,000 each with two sureties and the condition that they surrender their passports to the court.
Meanwhile, in a separate Sessions Court, Balamurugan, Saravanan and Gobinath pleaded not guilty before Judge Madihah Zainol to a charge of gang robbery against the Singaporean man.
They were charged with robbing the man of a gold necklace and a Rolex watch from a car in Johor Bahru Utara, at about 2 pm on Aug 8.
The charge was brought under Section 395 of the Penal Code which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and caning, if convicted. Nevina did not offer bail on the grounds that the offence was serious and could not be bailed.
However, the court allowed the three accused to be bailed at RM9,000 each with a local surety, in addition to conditions not to disturb the victim and prosecution witnesses, report to the nearest police station once a month and surrender their passports to the court if they have any.
In separate proceedings, Saravanan and Puganeswaran were fined RM3,000 after pleading guilty before Magistrate Nurzihan Abdul Rehman to a charge of causing injury to the Singaporean man by using a knife.
They are alleged to have committed the act at an apartment in Taman Skudai Baru, Skudai between 10 am and 1 pm on Aug 11.
The charge was brought under Section 324 of the Penal Code read together with Section 34 of the same code which provides for a jail sentence of up to 10 years or a fine or whipping, if convicted.
The court also ordered the accused to serve a six-month jail sentence if they fail to pay the fine.
All courts have set Sept 23 for mention of the case and appointment of lawyers. — Bernama

Title: High Court proceeds with Duta Enclave assessment as Semantan Estate weighs secret settlement terms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Putrajaya’s offer to compensate Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd without a formal assessment exercise remains open, though the company has yet to provide a response, according to a senior federal counsel.
The offer, made on Aug 14, is a strategic attempt by the government to settle the decades-long dispute over the 106-hectare “Duta Enclave.”
While the specific terms and financial value of the proposal remain undisclosed, the legal team representing the government is still waiting for a definitive answer, FMT reported.
“We do not know whether they are accepting or rejecting the offer as their lawyers have not reverted to us,” senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan told reporters following proceedings at the High Court today.
Last week, Semantan applied to postpone the hearing to evaluate the government’s proposal, but Justice Roslan Mat Nor rejected the application, allowing the assessment of compensation to proceed.
This comes after a landmark Court of Appeal ruling last year, which determined that the company is entitled to adequate compensation based on the land’s valuation at the time of its 1956 acquisition.
The appeals court also mandated an assessment of mesne profits — compensation for the loss of use of the property. The prime land, situated along Jalan Tuanku Abdul Halim, currently houses vital federal infrastructure, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Academy, the Inland Revenue Board, and the National Archives.
The legal saga began in 2003 when Semantan sued the government, alleging unlawful acquisition. While the Court of Appeal previously ruled that the land could not be returned due to the extensive government infrastructure built upon it, the Federal Court’s refusal to grant leave for further appeal paved the way for the current compensation assessment.
During today’s proceedings, Semantan’s sole witness, licensed property valuer Foo Gee Jen, faced cross-examination by Nurhafizza and fellow senior federal counsel Azza Azmi regarding his 1956 valuation.
The government’s legal team challenged Foo’s methodology, specifically his reliance on comparable property values from the Batu Estate and bungalow lots in Bukit Tunku.
The assessment of mesne profits is being handled in a separate hearing before High Court judge Ahmad Shahrir Salleh. Semantan is represented by lawyer Ira Biswas.
The court has adjourned the hearing until Sept 1.

Title: Anwar asks Indonesia’s Prabowo to intercede in Felda's RM2.5b PT Eagle High loss
Article:
BANGI, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reached out formally to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, requesting special intervention regarding Felda’s investments in Indonesia, specifically involving PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk (EHP).
The appeal follows the discovery of a potential large-scale financial loss amounting to RM2.5 billion, sustained as a result of decisions made by previous management.
Without a resolution, the returns the agency might eventually recover are estimated to be only around RM200 million,
Bernama
reported.
“This investment (EHP) is stuck in the courts in Indonesia. I have written a letter to President Prabowo Subianto asking him to also look into this problem. Then, if it is not addressed, of this RM2.5 billion, what we may eventually obtain is RM200 million. This is one example,” Anwar said.
The PM disclosed these details during a Friendly Session with Felda’s top management and managers today. He explained that the transparency regarding these fiscal figures is intended to ensure that the agency’s grassroots leadership fully understands the gravity of the challenges facing Felda.
While acknowledging that the financial burden does not fall directly on regional managers in states like Pahang or Johor, Anwar stressed that a collective understanding of the crisis is essential for a successful recovery.
“I want the managers to know, and how difficult it is to recover … it is not the managers’ problem. Felda managers in Pahang, in Johor, what does this (investment) have to do with them? But (the problem) is borne by us, that is the problem, so (everyone) must know,” he said.
Anwar urged management at all levels to ignore narratives or propaganda that attempt to downplay governance failures, insisting that the problems must be confronted head-on.
“I have repeatedly said that we bear this problem … the matter I need to emphasise is that I want Felda managers as a whole to truly digest the problems. It does not mean that sometimes they should feel weary or tired, but they must know that these problems must and have to be addressed,” he added.
As part of a comprehensive recovery plan, the PM said that the government is accelerating basic welfare projects. This includes immediate allocations for repairs to the homes of managers and settlers, ensuring these essential works are not postponed until the next budget cycle.
Anwar later emphasised that the focus on governance, integrity, and accountability is not a search for scapegoats, but a necessary step to safeguard public trust and restore Felda’s legacy as an institution of national pride.

Title: Anwar: Action against Tabung Haji, Felda based on wrongdoing, not religion or race
Article:
KAJANG, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected claims that the government’s scrutiny of Tabung Haji (TH) is driven by the institution’s Islamic identity, insisting that any action taken is a response to mismanagement and wrongdoing, not religious or racial targeting.
Speaking at a programme with Felda’s top management today, Anwar said the same principle applied across the board, citing Felda as another example of an institution closely associated with the Malay community that has faced government intervention over past failures,
FMT
reported.
“Some Islamic party leaders say action is mainly being taken against Malay-Muslim agencies. If issues are identified, we will take action. Don’t make this a racial or religious issue,” he said.
Although he did not name anyone directly, Anwar’s remarks come a day after PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang claimed that Muslims are less involved in corruption compared to non-Muslims, arguing that Islamic institutions such as Tabung Haji are singled out for scrutiny specifically because of their religious branding.
In his statement, Hadi had argued that faith served as a restraint on Muslims that made them less prone to graft, and alleged that enforcement in Malaysia has been selective, with senior figures and non-Muslim “cartels, black-market traders and smugglers” escaping consequences while others are unfairly targeted.
On TH specifically, Hadi had said he did not deny that wrongdoing occurred, but argued that similar or worse misconduct at government-linked companies goes unreported, contending that the fund’s Islamic branding makes it a target for headlines.
Anwar pushed back against this framing today, pointing to the government’s handling of Felda as proof that action against institutions linked to the Malay community is not about optics.
He noted that the government had tabled a white paper on Felda and set up a special task force and committee to prevent a repeat of the agency’s past problems, arguing this showed mismanagement would not be overlooked simply because an institution carries ethnic or religious significance.
The exchange adds to ongoing tension between the unity government and PAS over how corruption cases involving Malay-Muslim institutions are perceived and reported, with Hadi separately having taken aim at Pakatan Harapan’s broader anti-corruption record as ineffective.

Title: Government agency chairman among five remanded in MACC probe over alleged below-market land sale
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 21 — The Magistrate’s Court here today granted a four-day remand order for five individuals, including the chairman of a government agency with the title of Datuk, to assist in an investigation into suspected abuse of position involving the disposal of land.
Magistrate Noor Idayu Salim issued the remand order following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
The four other suspects comprise two company directors, a technical manager and a female clerk. They were detained by the MACC between 11am and noon yesterday while they were at the commission’s office to have their statements recorded.
The agency chairman, who is in his 50s, is alleged to have abused his position as Deputy Chairman and Board Member in 2015 to approve the sale of eight plots of land in South Seberang Perai to a company believed to be owned by an associate.
He is also alleged to have approved the sale at below-market value, resulting in an estimated loss of RM1.96 million.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted yesterday, saying the case was being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Penang Hill cable car hits 32pc completion; operations expected by late 2027
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 21 — The Penang Hill cable car project has reached 32 per cent completion and is expected to be physically finished by August next year, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today.
The state expects operations to commence in the final quarter of 2027.
Speaking during a monitoring visit from the Botanic Gardens to the summit of Penang Hill, Chow noted that the project has entered a more promising phase following the completion of all underground works. This progress includes the successful installation of the third tower.
“We expect the work to progress faster because above-ground construction is easier to control compared with underground works,” Chow said.
The underground phase has been very challenging, Chow said, as strict technical conditions and the rocky terrain of Penang Hill prohibited the use of heavy machinery, forcing contractors to rely on hand tools.
The RM367.2 million project, currently being implemented by Hartasuma Sdn Bhd, officially broke ground in January last year.
Chow stressed that the visible installation of the towers should reassure the public that the project is moving forward steadily despite initial delays.

Title: Felda task force to examine current management, not just past problems, says Anwar
Article:
BANGI, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would wait for the complete report of the Special Task Force investigating the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA) before making any official announcement.
He said the special task force had begun its work and the findings of the investigation were expected to be presented in the near future.
“The special task force has started and I am waiting for the investigation to be completed, then we will announce it shortly.
“(Its aspects include) all matters regarding management, improving management... of course identifying past problems, but what is important is current management and way forward,” he said.
He told reporters after officiating a Friendly Session with Felda Top Management and Managers at Tenera Hotel, here today.
Also present were Felda chairman Tan Sri Ahmad Badri Mohd Zahir and director-general Datuk Dr Suzana Idayu Wati Osman.
Previously, the media reported that the Special Task Force report on FELDA was expected to be completed in a few months before being made public.
Anwar said he would release the report to the public as soon as it was completed and asked the public to read it like the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the Tabung Haji (TH) Board. — Bernama

Title: Singaporean man jailed for insulting Islam during e-hailing trip in Johor Bahru
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 21 — A 56-year-old Singaporean man has been jailed for 14 days and fined RM7,000 after admitting to demeaning Islam during a trip in Johor Bahru last month.
Mohamed Anim Atam pleaded guilty to the charges before Magistrate A. Shaarmini. The court ordered the sentence to commence from the date of his arrest on Aug 18, failing which he would face three months in prison.
The incident occurred at approximately 5pm on July 30, as the accused travelled from Jalan Tun Razak to Jalan Meldrum.
While riding as a passenger in an e-hailing vehicle, Mohamed Anim allegedly described the Quran’s contents as lacking compassion and focused only on killing. His remarks were overheard by the driver, Muhamad Danial Haikal Nadzahakim, 29.
The driver subsequently uploaded a two-minute and 20-second video of the conversation to social media, which quickly went viral.
In the clip, the driver can be heard criticising the passenger’s views and cautioning him about the sensitivity of the remarks. The passenger was heard apologising to the driver before exiting the vehicle by the roadside.
Mohamed Anim, a security guard in Singapore, was charged under Section 29B, a specific provision addressing the deliberate intent to hurt the religious feelings of any person through words, sounds, or gestures. The section provides for a maximum of one year’s imprisonment, a fine, or both.
During the proceedings, the accused appealed for a fine, citing high blood pressure and ongoing divorce proceedings.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Eizlan Azhar requested a proportionate sentence, noting that the offence touched upon highly sensitive issues involving race, religion, and royalty (3R), and had caused significant public outcry via social media.
The case came to light after a police report was lodged on July 31. Mohamed Anim was later arrested at the Sultan Iskandar Building along Jalan Lingkaran Dalam, Bukit Chagar, at 4.15pm on Aug 18.

Title: Airbnb crackdown: Penang introduces new licensing laws for short-term rentals
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 20 — Penang has introduced a new regulatory framework to govern short-term rentals of private accommodations, including Airbnbs and homestays, effective August 1.
State local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye announced that the Penang Private Short-term Accommodation By-Laws 2026 now require all TIP operators to obtain official licences from their respective city councils.
“The by-laws will give both the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP) the authority to license operators and act against those who fail to comply,” H’ng said during a press conference at Komtar today.
To allow the industry to adjust, the state has granted a two-month grace period. Operators must submit their applications before enforcement begins on November 1.
H’ng noted that Penang is the first state in Malaysia to implement such specific by-laws. Previously, local authorities lacked the legal teeth to take action against unlicensed operators.
“Now, there is a clear legal basis for both local authorities to issue licences and take action against those who do not comply,” he added.
The move follows a surge in complaints. Between 2020 and March this year, MBPP received 364 complaints regarding public nuisance and safety issues linked to illegal TIPs, while MBSP recorded 24.
Under the new by-laws, a TIP is defined as paid accommodation provided without a tenancy agreement for a period not exceeding six consecutive months.
Certain properties are strictly prohibited from operating as TIPs, including government or statutory body premises; healthcare or childcare centres; workers’ hostels and private education institutions; low-cost and low-medium-cost housing, controlled-price homes; and People’s Housing Projects.
In the MBPP jurisdiction, all strata residential properties are barred from TIP operations, though this remains subject to the house rules of the respective management corporations.
While service apartments, SOHO units, and shophouses may operate as TIPs, they must still adhere to management rules. Landed properties, such as detached or terrace houses, may be considered provided the operator obtains planning permission to convert the building’s use.
Additionally, the state has designated “no-go” zones where TIPs are forbidden, including Jesselton Heights, Pearl Hill, Lebuh Bukit Jambul, Taman Sungai Ara, and Minden Heights.
Operators must pay an administrative fee of RM50 per application, with annual licence fees starting at RM1,000 for premises with up to three rooms. An additional RM200 is charged for each extra room, capped at two. Operators will also be subject to an annual TIP fee of RM1,800 per unit.
Those who defy the regulations face a fine of up to RM2,000, a jail term of up to one year, or both.

Title: Malaysia targets first ‘made by Malaysia’ chips using Arm Limited technology by 2030, says economy minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The government is targeting 2030 for the first “Made by Malaysia” chips developed using Arm Limited technology to enter production and the semiconductor supply chain.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said four companies have so far begun designing chips using technology from British semiconductor technology company Arm Limited, with the aim of eventually bringing their products into production and the semiconductor supply chain.
He said the companies were expected to take about three years to develop their products after gaining access to the relevant Arm technology, although the timeline would vary depending on the technology and market targeted.
“We hope the initial chip designs could be completed by 2028 before the companies move on to production and commercialisation,” he told a press conference at the Economy Ministry’s monthly assembly today.
“The development will take approximately about three years for them to come up with the chip.
“We are setting the target to produce the first one by 2030,” he added.
He added that the government wanted the chips not only to be designed locally but also to be produced and used in the semiconductor supply chain, subject to the companies’ ability to secure customers for their products.
In line with the target, the government today handed offer letters to Oppstar Technology Sdn Bhd and Alphaswift Industries Sdn Bhd for access to Arm Compute Subsystem (CSS) technology and the Arm Flexible Access (AFA) programme, respectively, under the strategic cooperation between Malaysia and Arm Limited.
Akmal said eight Arm technology-access packages — comprising four Arm CSS and four Arm Flexible Access tokens — had so far been offered to five local companies.
The access is intended to help local companies accelerate integrated circuit design and research and development activities in Malaysia, including in areas such as drones and advanced microelectronics.
He said each token provided access to different technologies, with companies assessed according to their technical capabilities, identified markets, potential customers and commercial prospects.
He added that the government was also seeking to ensure that the partnership generated benefits beyond chip design, including local manufacturing and the development of highly skilled Malaysian engineers.
“We want this access to global technology to be a catalyst for more chip designs, intellectual property and high-value products to be developed in Malaysia,” Akmal said.
“This is the foundation for producing local companies and engineers capable of bringing Malaysian chip products to the global market.”
1,530 have undergone Arm training
On talent development, Akmal said 1,530 participants had so far undergone Arm On-Demand Training, out of a target of training 10,000 people over four years.
He said the training was intended to give participants early exposure to Arm technology and create a talent pipeline that could eventually support companies involved in chip design, research and production.
When asked about expected salaries, the minister said some graduates of programmes conducted jointly with SIRIM’s Semiconductor Integrated Circuit Design and Application Centre (SIDAC) in Selangor had secured starting salaries of about RM5,500, potentially rising to between RM8,000 and RM9,000 after two to three years of experience.
Elaborating, he stressed that the 10,000-person target did not mean that all participants would immediately become highly specialised chip designers, but was instead intended to create a broader pool of talent familiar with Arm systems and semiconductor technologies.
He said the government also hopes that companies receiving access to Arm technology will recruit Malaysian talent for their design, research and production activities.
To strengthen the talent pipeline, the government has reached an agreement with 12 universities, supported by the ministry, government agencies and industry players, for a more structured implementation of the Arm On-Demand Training programme.

Title: Tiktoker under police probe after allegedly stepping on Sarawak flag
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 21 — A TikToker is being investigated after uploading a video showing a man allegedly disrespecting Sarawak by deliberately stepping on the Ibu Pertiwi flag.
Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the district police headquarters has received two reports regarding the incident.
“Initial investigation found that the five-second video was uploaded by the TikTok account user and was shared by several other social media accounts.
“The case is being investigated under Section 504 of the Penal Code for intentional insults meant to provoke a breach of the peace – which provides for imprisonment of up to two years, or a fine, or both if convicted,” he said in a statement.
The case is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for the misuse of network facilities and services to transmit online content deemed obscene, menacing, offensive, indecent, or false.
The Section provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000, or a year in prison, or both upon conviction.
Alexson advised the public not to take actions that could disrupt the peace, provoke, or incite public anger and unrest.
Those with further information on the incident can contact the Kuching District Police Headquarters on 082-244444.
The TikToker allegedly uploaded similar content previously before deleting it several hours later.
He is said to be no stranger to controversy, having reportedly harassed cosplayers at anime events
It is understood that the man is disabled. — The Borneo Post

Title: Putrajaya gears up for National Day bash, expects 80,000 visitors
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — More than 80,000 visitors are expected to flood Dataran Putrajaya in conjunction with National Day 2026, with preparations now reaching between 85 and 90 per cent.
Ministry of Communications secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said preparations involving various levels, including static training of all contingents, had begun in preparation for the celebration themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”.
“I need to inform you that the government has set the celebration this time with a modest allocation but we will still feel the excitement.
“The air show is still there but on a small scale, (parade) assets have also been reduced taking into account the global energy crisis and the government is very careful and cautious in managing this matter,” he told reporters after the Handover Ceremony from Perbadanan Putrajaya (PPj) in conjunction with the 2026 National Day Celebration here today.
Also present were PPj president Datuk Mohd Sakeri Abdul Kadir and chief ceremonial officer of the Government Ceremony and Secretariat Division of the International Conference Datuk Rozainor Ramli.
He said monitoring weather conditions was also a matter of attention, with collaboration held with the Malaysian Meteorological Department and the Department of Environment to obtain the latest information before it was presented to the public.
Earlier in his speech, he said the Ministry of Communications had established 18 working committees to ensure that all aspects of the celebration preparations were carried out in an orderly manner, and one of them was the Logistics and Venue Preparation Committee, which plays a strategic role in ensuring that the site readiness and all logistical requirements are at the best level.
“The readiness of the celebration site not only reflects the image and quality of the organisation, but is also an important aspect in ensuring that the entire event can take place smoothly, orderly and safely without any obstacles,” he said.
Towards the final phase of preparations, the rehearsal session for the 2026 National Day Celebration will take place for four days from August 26 to 29.
The procession and parade event will involve 10,819 participants from 77 contingents, in addition to featuring 328 assets, 22 electric vehicles (EVs), 112 live assets, 22 marching bands and 11 decorated cars. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji RCI probe: Former CEO arrives in Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court for remand
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A former chief executive officer of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here for remand proceedings related to investigations into a case linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on TH.
The man, in his 60s, arrived at 9.35 am wearing an orange Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) remand shirt.
The RCI Report on TH, uploaded on the official Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) portal on July 29, among other things, recommended that a forensic audit be conducted to examine how past investment decisions were made, which resulted in TH suffering a severe impairment in the value of its assets.
The RCI report, which investigated issues concerning TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, also listed problematic investments that require a forensic audit.
The RCI found evidence of suspicious transactions and concealment of information.
On July 30, MACC said it had established a special team to review and scrutinise the RCI report for any legal issues involving elements of corruption, misappropriation, document forgery, abuse of power or money laundering under the MACC Act 2009 and the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, or related offences. — Bernama

Title: Former Tabung Haji CEO remanded seven days in MACC probe linked to RCI findings
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief executive officer has reportedly been remanded for seven days to assist an investigation stemming from the findings of the royal commission of inquiry (RCI) into the pilgrims’ fund.
Berita Harian
reported that Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order, which runs until August 27, after allowing an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court this morning.
The unidentified man, who is reportedly in his 60s, arrived at the court at 9.38am wearing orange lock-up attire and handcuffs while being escorted by MACC officers.
Berita Harian
reported that the former CEO is also a prominent corporate figure who previously held positions at several leading companies.
Separately,
Malay Mail
reported on August 15 that MACC had detained seven people in investigations arising from the RCI report, comprising a shipping company CEO, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.
The 252-page RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, was declassified and released on July 29, four years after it was completed.
Among its recommendations were amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to bar active politicians from serving as directors of TH and its subsidiaries, and to introduce expertise requirements for board members.

Title: GOF raids seven illegal sand mining sites across three states, seizes RM13m worth of assets
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 21 — The General Operations Force (GOF) has cracked down on illegal mining activities after raiding seven separate locations in three states through Ops Gali Mega, with a total seizure value estimated at RM13.26 million.
GOF Central Brigade commander SAC Hakemal Hawari said the operation to crack down on the activities began at 11am yesterday, covering the areas of Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Johor.
He said a total of 31 individuals were checked in the operation, with 15 of them arrested for various offences.
Meanwhile, Hakemal said the latest raid at 3.30pm yesterday targeted an illegal operation site covering an area of 0.647 hectares at Lot PT 89, Jalan Lapangan Terbang Subang Lama, which is believed to be processing sand without permission.
He said the operation was carried out in an integrated manner with the cooperation of the Selangor Water Management Board (LUAS), the Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) and the Land and Mines Office (PTG).
“The raid at the site resulted in the arrest of 12 people consisting of five local men and seven foreign men.
“The operation team also seized 1,500 tonnes of sand, heavy machinery and sand washing and processing equipment with an estimated value of RM5 million at this location alone,” he said after visiting the illegal site after the raid here last night.
Touching on the syndicate’s modus operandi, Hakemal said the sand was believed to be brought in from outside areas including construction site waste to be washed and processed into fine sand, before being sold at a price of around RM500 to RM600 per lorry.
He said the sand processing activities, which usually operate during the day, also released soil washing waste directly into the nearby river, thus causing significant water pollution and turbidity.
He said all arrests were being investigated in accordance with the National Land Code Act 1965, the LUAS Enactment 1999, the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the By-Laws Act 2021.
Hakemal stressed that his party would not compromise with any party found to be involved in illegal activities.
In this regard, he called on the public to continue to channel information to the police if they find any suspicious activities in their respective areas. — Bernama

Title: Dengue cases surge 56pc as MOH warns of nationwide spread
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has sounded the alarm over a significant surge in dengue cases across Malaysia, with infections spiking by more than 50 per cent compared to last year.
Data as of Epidemiological Week 32 (EW 32/2026) reveals a total of 58,079 reported cases, or a 56.2 per cent increase from the same period in 2025.
The crisis has already claimed 55 lives due to complications from the virus, MOH said.
While initial clusters were centred in the Klang Valley, specifically across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya, the ministry warns that the risk is no longer contained.
Despite intensive prevention measures and the mobilisation of field personnel in the capital, an upward trend is now being detected in several other states.
Health officials attribute this rise to Malaysia's current volatile weather patterns. The cycle of intermittent rainfall and intense heat has created an ideal breeding ground for Aedes mosquitoes. Compounding the issue is the high volume of poorly maintained water-holding containers found in and around residential areas.
The ministry stressed that dengue control is a collective responsibility, particularly as more than 70 per cent of Aedes breeding sites are still located within residential premises.
To combat the spread, MOH is calling for a unified effort from all sectors: including government agencies, local authorities, the private sector, and individual households. Every Malaysian must take ownership of their surroundings to ensure they are free from mosquito traps.
The public is urged to commit at least 10 minutes every week to inspect and destroy potential breeding sites in their homes.
Residents should also take proactive measures to prevent mosquito bites and seek medical attention immediately if they experience fever or any dengue warning signs.

Title: Any lane, any time: Plus activates JustGo ANPR toll payments across North-South Expressway minus Penang Bridge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Plus Malaysia has activated its JustGo toll payment system across the entire North-South Expressway (NSE) network, except the Penang Bridge, using automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to allow motorists to pay tolls through any available lane.
The nationwide rollout follows a successful pilot phase in early 2026. This development is a major leap in the operator’s efforts to modernise toll collection and provide a more seamless transit experience for millions of highway users.
Under the JustGo framework, a registered vehicle’s plate number anchors the payment process.
As a car enters a toll plaza, ANPR cameras identify the vehicle and process the transaction via the payment method linked to the user’s JustGo account. This effectively eliminates the need for drivers to queue for dedicated RFID or Touch 'n Go lanes, as the technology functions across all lanes.
To activate the service, motorists must
download the JustGo app on Android or iOS
and register their vehicle plate number.
The registration process requires users to upload a digital vehicle ownership certificate, which can be retrieved from the Road Transport Department (JPJ) app. Finally, a debit or credit card must be linked within the JustGo app to facilitate automated billing.
The system is designed for flexibility, allowing a single JustGo account to manage up to 10 different vehicles. This makes it a convenient solution for households or fleet managers handling multiple cars under one digital roof.
Plus argues that the activation of JustGo is a move toward reducing dependence on physical on-board units or tags. It serves as a precursor to a broader transition toward a Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) system, which aims to eventually remove physical barriers at toll plazas entirely.
Despite the network-wide launch, JustGo remains unavailable on the Penang Bridge. Motorists travelling to or from Penang Island via the bridge must continue using existing payment methods for the time being. Plus has yet to announce a specific timeline for the technology's extension to the bridge.

Title: Anwar impressed by Sukma’s young athletes, hopes to see them represent country
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes the young athletes competing in the 2026 Selangor Malaysia Games (Sukma) will go on to represent Malaysia on the international stage.
In a Facebook post last night, Anwar said he was impressed by the spirit, discipline and courage displayed by the young athletes when he had the opportunity to meet them and watch the Muay Thai events.
“Hopefully, they will one day have the opportunity to represent Malaysia and make the country proud on the international stage,” he said.
Selangor is hosting the biennial games again after 28 years, with more than 5,000 young athletes from across the country competing for 468 gold medals in 37 sports until August 24. — Bernama

Title: Two cyclists die in Putrajaya after vehicle hits them while changing lanes, say police
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — Two cyclists died after being hit by a vehicle at kilometre 9.0 of Jalan Persiaran Selatan, Putrajaya, last night, said Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed.
In a statement today, Aidi Sham said the accident occurred at 10.15pm, involving a vehicle driven by a local man in his 40s and two male cyclists aged in their 40s and 30s respectively.
“Initial investigations found that the vehicle being driven had changed direction from the middle lane to the left lane before hitting the two cyclists.
“As a result of the accident, both cyclists were confirmed dead at the scene of the accident due to severe injuries to their face and head,” he said.
He said investigations were continuing under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Therefore, he asked the public or witnesses to the incident who had relevant information to come forward to assist in the investigation by contacting the Putrajaya Traffic Police Station at 03-88862138 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Serian API hits ‘Very Unhealthy’ level of 241 as Sarawak air quality worsens
Article:
SERIAN, Aug 21 — Air quality here is still at a very unhealthy level with the monitoring station at the Serian District Police Headquarters registering an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 241 as of 8am on Friday.
The Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website also showed eight monitoring stations in Sarawak registering unhealthy readings.
Topping the list was Sri Aman with 189, followed by Kuching (186), Samarahan (179), Sarikei (173), Sibu (156), Bintulu (154), Samalaju (145), and Kapit (129).
The DoE’s four other monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded moderate API readings – with 96 registered in Mukah, 77 in both Miri and ILP Miri, and 63 in Limbang.
The worsening API in Serian is largely due to transboundary haze from West Kalimantan in Indonesia.
The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) in an update at 5.32pm on Thursday said dry conditions prevailed over most parts of the southern Asean region except over the northern parts of Borneo where some showers were observed.
Scattered to widespread hotspots were detected in Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra, while few to isolated hotspots were detected elsewhere in the southern Asean region.
As of Thursday, there were 298 hotspots detected in Kalimantan –  based on the daily hotspot count from Aug 14-20.
The highest number of hotspots in Kalimantan were recorded on Aug 18 when 1,079 hotspots were detected.
The centre said moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes were observed emanating from hotspot clusters in West Kalimantan, drifting northwards into the western and central parts of Sarawak.
“Moderate to dense smoke plumes were also observed to emanate from hotspot clusters detected in many parts of Kalimantan and the southern parts of Sumatra.
“Several air quality stations in West and South Kalimantan, as well as the western and central parts of Sarawak recorded unhealthy levels,” said ASMC.
However, it pointed out that the full extent of the hotspot and smoke haze situation in the region could not be determined due to cloud cover.
On the weather and haze outlook, ASMC said dry conditions are expected over most parts of the southern Asean region in the coming days, except over the northern parts of Borneo and the northern and western parts of Sumatra where showers are forecast.
As such, it said the hotspot and smoke haze situation could continue to escalate in areas experiencing prolonged periods of dry weather, with a continued risk of transboundary haze occurrence.
“The prevailing winds over the southern Asean region are forecast to blow from the southeast to southwest.
“On the other hand, wet weather is expected to persist over the northern Asean region, which helps to keep the hotspot and smoke haze situation subdued,” it added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Police hunt suspects after attempted armed robbery of Klang gold shop leaves one injured
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 21 — Police are hunting for suspects believed to be involved in an attempted robbery of a gold shop at Jalan Tengku Kelana, Klang, near here, yesterday morning, which has gone viral on social media.
Klang Selatan district deputy police chief Supt Kamalariffin Aman Shah confirmed the incident.
He said the incident, which occurred at about 10.30am, is also believed to have caused injuries to an individual and involved the use of firearms.
“Klang Selatan district police headquarters (IPD) Criminal Investigation Division has opened an investigation paper under Section 394 of the Penal Code for causing hurt during an attempted gang robbery.
“The case is also being investigated under Section 4 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971 for displaying firearms while attempting to commit robbery,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Kamalarifin urged members of the public with information to contact investigating officer Insp Mohamad Sulaimi Alawi @ Shaari at 014-5719405 or the Klang Selatan IPD Operations Room at 03-33762222, or the nearby police station.
Earlier, a video circulating on social media showed several individuals armed with hammers entering a gold shop and smashing its display glass, believed to be in an attempt to commit robbery, but they failed and fled on motorcycles. — Bernama

Title: MCMC: Scammers turn to RCS, iMessage after hyperlink restrictions on SMS
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 21 — Online scams have been detected shifting to messaging services such as Rich Communication Services (RCS) and iMessage to spread phishing links following the enforcement of hyperlink restrictions on short messaging service (SMS).
Selangor Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Telecommunications Fraud deputy director Mohd Amirul Hakim Abdul Rahim said the shift was detected as these messaging services still allowed the transmission of hyperlinks to users for phishing purposes.
Besides RCS and iMessage, phishing links are also being spread through over-the-top (OTT) services such as WhatsApp and Telegram.
“For SMS, MCMC has enforced a directive for telecommunications companies prohibiting hyperlinks, requests to call back numbers or requests for personal details through official SMS... so they (scammers) shifted to RCS and iMessage.
“Accordingly, MCMC will engage with these platform providers to explore measures that can be implemented, including approaches similar to the restrictions applied to SMS,” he said when appearing as a panellist at the ‘National Digital Scam Forum: Threat to National Financial Security and Mule Accounts’ here yesterday.
The forum was held in conjunction with the 2026 National Anti-Scam Awareness Programme launched by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Besides the MCMC representative, the forum featured National Financial Crime Centre (NFCC) director-general Datuk Seri Shamshun Baharin Mohd Jamil, Selangor Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) chief SAC Mohamad Rosni Mohamed Lazim and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) LINK and Offices Department (JLPB) deputy director Hasjun Hashim as panellists.
Meanwhile, Mohd Amirul said that for content suspected of containing fraudulent elements, such as illegal investments or impersonation of financial institutions, MCMC would verify it with relevant agencies before taking action to block or take down the content.
He said investment-related cases would be referred to the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC), while cases involving banking would be verified with BNM or the relevant banking institutions.
He added that if the content or account was confirmed to be linked to fraudulent activity, blocking action would be taken against the affected channels, including messaging, cellular or SMS services, to prevent it from reaching users.
Meanwhile, Hasjun advised the public to remain vigilant against scam syndicates tricking individuals into opening companies as part of tactics related to mule accounts.
She said opening an account online, particularly with digital banks, was subject to the electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC) process to verify the applicant’s identity using identification documents and facial recognition.
“Now their modus operandi is to tell (victims) to open a company. For digital banks, account opening is indeed done online because they do not have branches, but there is a process that must be carried out through e-KYC.
“That process is to ensure that the individual opening the account is really that person, and the process is supposed to be very strict,” she said.
Hasjun said individuals who found that a bank account has been opened without their presence or consent should lodge a complaint with the bank concerned to enable an investigation into the account opening process.
She said every bank and insurance company had a dedicated complaints unit to handle cases that could not be resolved at the branch or service centre level.
“If you do not get a satisfactory answer or do not receive a response from the bank after 14 days, you can come to Bank Negara,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Kuantan police corporal jailed nine months after Court of Appeal reinstates RM700 bribery conviction
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A corporal with the police force began serving a nine-month jail term yesterday after the Court of Appeal reinstated his conviction and sentence for accepting a RM700 bribe to release a suspect in a ketum water case.
A three-judge panel, comprising Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, also upheld the Sessions Court’s order that Mohamed Syaffiq Mohamed Sidek, 36, pay a RM10,000 fine, or serve 12 months’ jail in default.
The panel allowed the prosecution’s cross-appeal and dismissed Mohamed Syaffiq’s appeal against his conviction and sentence. He had previously obtained a stay of execution pending his appeal.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Noorin said the appellant had admitted to receiving the RM700 but failed to prove it was for any purpose other than graft.
Justice Noorin said the court had considered the full circumstances surrounding the transaction, notably that the money was handed over outside the police station, not in a social context, and that it came from the suspect’s friend to the appellant.
She noted that the receipt of the RM700 was not only supported by prosecution witnesses but also admitted by the appellant himself.
“Once the fact of receipt is established, the precondition under Section 50(1) is met, and the statutory presumption as to the nature and purpose of the payment arises,” she said.
On May 3, 2023, the Kuantan Sessions Court convicted Mohamed Syaffiq of accepting the bribe from Afiq Hidayatullah Hussin to release Muhammad Faiz Aiman Mohd Yusof for the possession of ketum water.
The offence was committed at the Kuantan Police Station, Jalan Mahkota, Kuantan, Pahang, between 1.00pm and 2.00pm on December 25, 2020.
On December 9, 2025, the High Court allowed Mohamed Syaffiq’s appeal, quashing his conviction and sentence under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009, and substituting it with a conviction under Section 165 of the Penal Code, with a one-month jail term.
In yesterday’s proceedings, MACC deputy public prosecutors Dr. Ifa Sirrhu Samsudin and Ezuain Farhana Ahmad appeared for the prosecution.
Lawyers Datuk Sukri Mohamed, Melissa Sukri and Shahidah Muslimah Roslan represented Mohamed Syaffiq. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Immigration repatriates 4,750 undocumented migrants so far this year
Article:
TAWAU, Aug 21 — The Sabah Immigration Department has repatriated 4,750 illegal immigrants of various nationalities to their respective countries so far this year.
In a statement yesterday, the Sabah Immigration Department said Filipinos accounted for the highest number at 3,008, followed by Indonesians (1,478), Pakistanis (118), Chinese (109), Vietnamese (18) and 19 others of various nationalities.
“The figure also includes the latest transfer programme involving 144 Indonesian nationals (yesterday) who were transported via the route using a commercial ferry,” it said.
The statement said all the Indonesian detainees, aged between three and 68, comprised 107 adult men, 26 adult women, four boys and seven girls, with the children accompanied by their parents or respective escorts.
All of them, from the Kota Kinabalu, Papar and Sandakan Immigration Detention Depots, were transferred after completing their sentences under the relevant legal provisions and obtaining valid Travel Documents in Lieu of Passport (SPLP).
“The Immigration Department of Malaysia urges all parties to be more vigilant about their surroundings in the community, refrain from colluding to protect or employ illegal immigrants and immediately report any activities involving illegal immigrants through official channels,” it said.
The Sabah Immigration Department urged the public to channel any information or complaints regarding illegal immigrant activities through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) portal or the Online Enquiry System (SPO). — Bernama

Title: Penang land scandal: MACC arrests government agency chairman, four others over undervalued sales
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained five individuals, including the chairman of a government agency, for allegedly exploiting their positions in the disposal of eight plots of land in Penang.
The suspects, aged between their 40s and 50s, include a chairman with a Datuk title, two company directors, a technical manager, and a clerk,
TV3
reported.
Sources indicate that the chairman allegedly abused his dual roles as deputy chairman and board member in 2015 to sanction the sale of eight plots of land in Seberang Perai Selatan.
The buyer is believed to be a company linked to one of his associates.
Investigators suspect the land was significantly undervalued during the transaction, causing the government agency to incur losses of approximately RM1.96 million.
The five suspects were arrested separately at the Penang MACC office between 11am and noon yesterday. They are expected to be produced before the Georgetown Magistrates’ Court this morning for a remand application.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests, saying that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for abuse of power.

Title: Fadhlina pushes swift investigation into alleged bullying, racial discrimination at KL school after student’s death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Schools Inspectorate, District Education Office and Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department have been directed to promptly complete an internal investigation into the alleged bullying and discrimination at a school here recently.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said matters of public concern, including those related to bullying and racial elements, must be taken seriously and addressed promptly based on facts and due processes.
“My thoughts and sympathies remain with the family and the school community following the recent passing of a school student in Kuala Lumpur.
“The Ministry of Education (MOE) is extending full cooperation to the police and working closely with the Social Welfare Department and the Ministry of Health to ensure that this matter is thoroughly addressed,” she said in a Facebook post.
At the same time, Fadhlina said attention and appropriate support were also being provided to the affected families, students, teachers and the entire school community.
She said the family of the deceased student had been provided with psychosocial support by the MOE counselling team, while teachers had been briefed on the ongoing investigation and legal processes, in addition to ensuring that their welfare and well-being continued to be given attention.
“The MOE Smart Support Team has also been mobilised to provide psychosocial support and crisis intervention to affected students to safeguard their welfare and emotional well-being.
“Our priority is to ensure justice for all parties and to take appropriate measures to ensure that the educational environment remains safe and free from any form of bullying and discrimination,” she said. — Bernama
